title: Make frontend adoption tests hermetic under parallel full-suite execution
description:
## Current state

Audited against master `4ef2e902` on 2026-09-07. Frontend permission and install-lock fixtures still exist; historical intermittent failures need a current controlled reproduction.

## Implementation

Isolate permission changes, package-manager store paths and dependency locks per fixture; restore permissions and owned resources through RAII on success and panic. Coordinate only source-file layout with the separate install-locking split task.

## Entry points

- `crates/jig/src/bootstrap/tests/frontend_adoption/pnpm.rs`
- `crates/jig/src/bootstrap/tests/frontend_adoption/install_locking.rs`

## Validation

Run focused tests for the changed behavior, then build `cargo build -p jig-sh --bin jig` and use `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig work check --plan-id <implementation-plan>` for applicable repository gates. Finish backend changes with `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test`. Use generic isolated fixtures; no live services or credentials are required unless explicitly identified as an external prerequisite.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run frontend adoption pnpm and install_locking fixtures in the frontend partition with isolated stores, then under controlled parallel nextest load. Capture EROFS path ownership and dependency-lock verification before teardown. A fresh failure is not claimed by this audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

Record exact current reproduction commands, fixture readiness signals, concurrency and observed failure classification. Regression must fail for the demonstrated old race and pass repeatedly under bounded isolated and concurrent runs. Preserve the timeout/ownership/permission/content oracle; do not skip the test, accept the failure, or merely inflate wall-clock thresholds. Run the owning partition and full backend gate after changes.

title: Make Jig a stack-neutral monorepo control plane
description:
## Outcome

Jig becomes a stack-neutral monorepo control plane through authored repository contracts and one Jig-owned planning and execution model.

## Stack-Neutral Invariant

Components describe repository boundaries, actions describe commands, and profiles compose actions. Languages, frameworks, package managers, infrastructure tools, and application platforms are fixture inputs and leaf programs, never contract concepts. Supporting another stack must require authored configuration and ordinary command execution, not a Jig core feature or schema branch.

## Active Scope

Consolidate reusable setup for existing v6 acceptance behavior without centralizing feature-specific assertions, make adoption component authoring candidate-based and exclusion-aware, migrate this repository to v6, add a foreground repository action command over the existing execution service, and introduce only the string argument and literal argv authority required by concrete actions. Scale target freshness in a separate compatible contract epoch using the existing action input paths plus explicit completeness policy. Let dev apps optionally reuse serve-target launch authority after literal argv runners exist.

## Adoption Boundary

Repository discovery proposes component candidates; it does not make every package manifest production authority. Adoption preview reports candidate roots, detection evidence, disposition, and explicit exclusions before write. Ambiguous candidates are not promoted by default. Discovery heuristics and exclusion inputs remain bootstrap concerns rather than runtime contract semantics; after adoption, authored components are authoritative.

## Dev Boundary

A dev app may reference a serve target to reuse argv, cwd, and base environment. Dev configuration remains authoritative for host, port, proxy, readiness, and session behavior. The existing dev supervisor remains the lifecycle owner; dev sessions do not become durable repository runs. Legacy inline dev configuration remains compatible.

## CI Boundary

A ci profile is an ordinary authored profile usable through the same CLI and MCP execution paths as any other profile. This epic does not generate or collapse repository CI workflows. Required-check names, job topology, service setup, matrices, migration base references, infrastructure jobs, and provider details remain repository-owned.

## Product Boundary

Reuse the existing repository catalog, planner, durable run model, receipts, gates, adapter descriptors, EvidenceReference DTOs, bootstrap inference/reporting, and dev supervisor. Do not introduce a second action graph, runtime language or framework model, Vite-specific contract semantics, adapter protocol, universal CI renderer, durable dev-run model, evidence vocabulary, cache, remote executor, or orchestration engine.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing v6 fixture construction is shared only where current behavior is genuinely common; feature-specific assertions remain with their owning tasks.
- Adoption previews candidate evidence and explicit exclusions; manifest presence alone does not author a component.
- Ambiguous or excluded candidates are not promoted, and authored components remain authoritative after adoption.
- Stack examples remain opaque components and commands; adding another ecosystem requires configuration rather than Jig core changes.
- Jig itself resolves as authored contract v6 with compatible developer workflows.
- Foreground CLI and MCP share the same planner and durable execution semantics.
- Dev apps may reuse serve-target argv, cwd, and base environment without transferring dev lifecycle ownership into durable runs.
- Legacy inline dev configuration remains compatible, and no Vite-specific contract semantics are added.
- Authored profiles, including ci, remain ordinary CLI and MCP inputs and do not generate workflow topology.
- The argument and runner epoch adds only proven string argument declarations, literal argv, and explicit compatibility shell authority.
- A separate freshness epoch uses ActionSpec.inputs as the sole path set plus explicit completeness policy and conservative fallback.
- No runtime language model, adapter protocol, universal CI renderer, generalized argument type system, second freshness path list, evidence store, artifact subsystem, multi-owner migration model, cache, remote execution, or delegated orchestrator is introduced.

title: Dogfood contract v6 and consolidate stack-neutral acceptance fixtures
description:
## Outcome

Jig dogfoods its generic v6 component, action, and profile model, backed by shared stack-neutral acceptance behavior and exclusion-aware adoption authoring.

## Scope

Inventory the existing v6 bootstrap and runtime fixtures and extract reusable construction or assertions only for behavior that already exists. Keep feature-specific assertions with their owners: exclusion-aware adoption behavior belongs to `.1.3`, while the repository v6 cutover and workflow-preservation checks belong to `.1.2`. After those tasks land, remove redundant fixture helpers only where actual reuse is demonstrated. Exercise materially different repository topologies through the same generic component, action, dependency, and profile semantics without turning ecosystem examples into contract concepts.

## Stack-Neutral Boundary

No language, framework, package manager, infrastructure tool, mobile platform, or desktop platform is required by the contract. A new ecosystem must fit through authored components and ordinary actions without core code or schema changes. Adoption-time detection evidence does not become runtime contract semantics.

## Boundaries

Do not make a shared harness responsible for unimplemented feature behavior. Do not add language-specific contract fields, an unbounded discovery engine, runtime exclusion semantics, external adapters, target-backed dev apps within this feature, persistent evidence storage, multi-owner migrations, or scoped freshness here.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing v6 fixture coverage is inventoried before shared setup changes.
- Shared construction and assertions cover only existing generic behavior that applies unchanged across materially different topology scenarios.
- Candidate, exclusion, write, and recopy regressions remain owned by .1.3.
- The Jig repository v6 cutover and workflow-preservation regressions remain owned by .1.2.
- Ecosystem examples remain opaque fixture content and no language or framework is a contract requirement.
- Redundant fixture construction is removed only where actual reuse is demonstrated.
- Existing v5 compatibility coverage remains intact and focused tests plus freshly built JIG_DEV_BIN contract and test gates pass.

title: Add exclusion-aware component candidate authoring to adoption
description:
## Outcome

Adoption proposes reviewable component candidates and requires explicit inclusion or exclusion decisions where repository evidence is ambiguous, so incidental package manifests do not become production components.

## Evidence

Inspected non-Jig repositories contain plausible Cargo and JavaScript package manifests beneath mocks, experiments, videos, marketing sites, and support tools. Raw manifest presence is therefore insufficient production-component authority.

## Scope

Extend the existing bounded, Git-aware adoption scan and inference report rather than adding a second discovery engine. Emit deterministic component candidates with repository-relative root, proposed identity, detection signals and sources, confidence, and disposition: included, explicitly excluded, or review required. Accept adoption-only exact-root exclusions through interactive or noninteractive answer inputs and show their effect in human and JSON previews. Begin with exact roots; do not introduce a general glob or ignore language without further evidence.

Existing workspace membership, explicit answers, and high-confidence repository structure may justify inclusion. A standalone manifest hit alone does not: ambiguous candidates remain visible as review required and are not authored by default. An adoption write authors only accepted candidates. Exclusion inputs and detection heuristics remain at the bootstrap boundary and do not become runtime component, affected-ignore, planner, or execution semantics. Once adopted, checked-in authored components remain authoritative for update or recopy. This task owns its candidate, exclusion, write, and recopy regression assertions.

## Compatibility

Preserve existing explicit component answers and supported high-confidence adoption behavior. Existing repositories without exclusion inputs continue to preview safely; ambiguous newly visible candidates are reported rather than silently promoted.
acceptance_criteria:
- Adoption preview deterministically reports candidate root, proposed identity, evidence, confidence, disposition, and reason in human and JSON output.
- Adoption-only exact-root exclusions are explicit and validated.
- A raw Cargo.toml or package.json hit is insufficient to author a component.
- Ambiguous and excluded candidates remain visible but are not promoted by default.
- Writes consume the reviewed decisions, while update and recopy preserve authored components without rediscovery.
- Existing bounded Git-aware scan and inference metadata are reused.
- Exclusions do not become runtime contract, planner, affected-ignore, or execution semantics.
- Generic fixtures cover production and incidental manifest trees without private identifiers.

title: Add a generic repository action execution surface
description:
## Outcome

Humans, agents, and automation execute authored repository actions through one Jig-owned planner, safety model, foreground CLI, MCP surface, and durable runtime.

## Scope

Add `jig run` over the existing execution service. Replace the migration-specific argument wire shape with the minimum declared string argument semantics required by the current migration-add action. Then activate a dedicated runner contract epoch for literal direct argv and explicit compatibility shell execution. Preserve effects, approvals, source identity, leases, cancellation, deterministic plans, target results, receipts, and legacy command-backed v6 repositories.

Target freshness is not part of this contract epoch; feature `.4` owns a separate compatible freshness epoch and does not block the foreground execution surface.

## Product Boundary

Jig owns selection, planning, dependency layers, execution, and result accounting. Ecosystem programs are declared leaf implementations. No caller-provided shell, generalized argument type system, freshness schema, cache, remote execution, dev-session ownership, or artifact policy is included.
acceptance_criteria:
- jig run and MCP share planning, safety, durable execution, and target results.
- Only named string arguments required by concrete actions are declared and normalized into plan identity.
- Migration-add uses the declared argument mechanism without waiting for an argv runner.
- A dedicated runner epoch distinguishes literal argv from explicit compatibility shell execution and binds only already-declared arguments.
- Freshness authority remains in feature .4 and does not block foreground execution.
- Legacy v6 command runners remain compatible.

title: Add foreground jig run over the shared repository execution service
description:
## Outcome

A human-facing foreground `jig run` command executes repository plans through the same Jig-owned service used by MCP, without duplicating transport logic or delegating orchestration.

## Scope

Extract a transport-neutral Jig execution service and add selectors, profiles, affected mode, explain, plan IDs, fail-fast, JSON output, cancellation, status, and exact repeated effect approvals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Equivalent CLI and MCP requests produce the same RunPlan and durable target results and receipts.
- Explain creates no run, lease, or effect approval.
- Effectful execution requires explicit selectors and exact --approve-effect worktree/external flags; there is no broad --yes bypass.
- Foreground cancellation cleans up Jig-owned child processes and leaves a truthful terminal run state.
- Repository dependency layers and target result accounting remain owned by Jig.
- Pre-v6 repositories receive an actionable migration diagnostic.

title: Declare minimal string action arguments and binding semantics
description:
## Outcome

Actions declare the smallest deterministic parameter surface required by current repository operations.

## Scope

Replace the migration-specific wire shape with named string argument declarations on `ActionSpec`, required and optional presence, conservative length validation, target-qualified CLI and MCP binding, and deterministic plan hashing. Migrate the existing migration-add name authority to this declared mechanism, including its Jig-native runner binding.

Direct argv runner discriminants and literal argv binding positions are owned by `.3.3`; this task must not implement or specify freshness authority.

## Boundaries

Do not add boolean, integer, choice, JSON, secret, arbitrary command, variadic, shell-interpolated, or freshness arguments. Add another type only with a named action that cannot be represented safely as a string.
acceptance_criteria:
- Named string arguments are declared on ActionSpec and validated consistently across source, resolved contract, CLI, MCP, planning, and Jig-native execution.
- Unknown, missing, duplicate, empty when forbidden, oversized, and unselected-target arguments fail before plan creation.
- Normalized values participate in deterministic plan identity.
- Migration-add name authority uses the declared mechanism and legacy no-argument actions remain unchanged.
- Direct argv runner kinds and binding positions remain owned by .3.3.
- No additional argument types or freshness fields are introduced.

title: Activate an argv and explicit-shell contract epoch
description:
## Outcome

A dedicated repository-contract epoch activates literal direct-argv execution and explicit compatibility shell authority while reusing the declared string argument semantics from `.3.2`.

## Scope

Add argv and shell runner discriminants, declare literal binding positions for already-declared string arguments, and migrate generated sources to the new runner epoch. Retain v6 command-key compatibility and ensure older runtimes cannot silently select the new schema. This task owns runner execution, binding, source and resolved schema migration, and runner-choice recopy compatibility; it does not add a second argument declaration mechanism.

Freshness authority belongs to feature `.4` and its separate compatible contract epoch.

## Product Boundary

Every runner is a leaf implementation inside a Jig-owned plan. Runner configuration cannot supply a competing graph, schedule, result lifecycle, cache, freshness claim, or remote executor.
acceptance_criteria:
- Literal argv execution never passes programs, fixed arguments, or bound declared values through shell parsing.
- Explicit shell runners accept no argument interpolation.
- Runner binding reuses the declarations and validation introduced by .3.2 rather than creating a second argument mechanism.
- The runner epoch preserves Jig planning, effects, approvals, source validation, cancellation, durable state, and target results.
- v6 command-key sources and resolved contracts remain readable, and recopy preserves authored runner choice.
- No freshness schema, additional argument types, output declarations, caching, remote execution, or delegated runner protocol is introduced.

title: Scale target evidence freshness by declared authority
description:
## Outcome

Unrelated monorepo changes no longer invalidate target evidence when a target explicitly declares its existing action inputs complete for freshness, while plans and running actions retain whole-repository staleness and mutation safety.

## Scope

Introduce a versioned freshness policy that marks the existing `ActionSpec.inputs` path set as exhaustive. Absence of that policy retains repository-wide conservative freshness. Do not add a parallel `freshness_inputs` list. Define transitive dependency and runner authority, establish a reproducible baseline on an anonymized large-repository fixture, activate a separate compatible freshness contract epoch, compute correct target-scoped identities, and cut new receipts and gates over with conservative legacy fallback. Reuse source observation across targets when straightforward. Add batching or other performance machinery only when measurements demonstrate material repeated-walk cost.

## Product Boundary

Jig computes freshness only from checked-in contracts and its own executions. Missing completeness policy, ambiguous, failed, unsupported, or excessive authority is unknown or stale, never fresh.

## Not In Scope

A second path-authority list, persistent full logs, content-addressed evidence storage, declared output or artifact manifests, archival lifecycle, cache reuse, remote stores, execution skipping, remote execution, elaborate symlink or submodule projection, and a dedicated performance service are not part of this feature.
acceptance_criteria:
- A versioned policy marks the existing ActionSpec.inputs set exhaustive for freshness; no parallel freshness_inputs list is added.
- Missing completeness policy retains repository-wide conservative freshness.
- A reproducible baseline demonstrates unrelated-change invalidation and records source-observation behavior.
- Complete scoped declarations ignore unrelated paths and invalidate on direct inputs, transitive dependencies, or runner authority.
- Missing, failed, ambiguous, or unsupported authority never reports fresh.
- Whole-repository plan and mutation safety remains unchanged.
- Legacy journals remain readable without false freshness.
- Correct target-scoped identities are implemented before performance machinery, and further optimization requires measured repeated-walk cost.

title: Specify conservative freshness policy over canonical action inputs
description:
## Outcome

An implementation-ready contract design distinguishes affected-selection hints from exhaustive target freshness authority without duplicating path declarations.

## Scope

Specify a versioned freshness policy that can mark the existing `ActionSpec.inputs` path set exhaustive. Policy absence retains repository-wide conservative freshness. Define transitive action authority, command and Jig-native runner authority contributions, digest domains, typed `TargetFreshness` states, and compatibility requirements for old plans, runs, receipts, and append-only journals.

This task owns the semantics and compatibility design only. It must not introduce `freshness_inputs`, implement fingerprint collection, migrate plan or journal schemas, or cut gates over; `.4.2` and `.4.3` own those implementation steps.
acceptance_criteria:
- ActionSpec.inputs remains the sole declared path set for both affected selection and freshness evaluation.
- A versioned explicit policy marks that path set exhaustive; policy absence remains repository-wide conservative.
- The design covers transitive action dependencies and selected runner authority in a versioned digest domain.
- Typed freshness states fail conservatively for unknown, unsupported, ambiguous, or failed authority.
- Compatibility requirements ensure old plans, runs, receipts, and journals remain readable without gaining false freshness.
- No freshness_inputs field, fingerprint implementation, plan or journal migration, or gate cutover is introduced by this specification task.

title: Implement correct target source and authority fingerprints
description:
## Outcome

The separate freshness contract epoch and evidence collection compute correct deterministic target-scoped identities without committing to unsupported filesystem projection or premature performance architecture.

## Entry Evidence

Before optimizing collection, add a reproducible anonymized repository fixture of roughly 4,000 files that demonstrates unrelated-change invalidation and records source-observation counts or elapsed instrumentation as target counts increase. Use the baseline only to decide whether repeated repository walks are materially costly.

## First Implementation

- Activate the freshness policy specified by `.4.1` while keeping `ActionSpec.inputs` as the sole path declaration.
- Add versioned plan identity and additive journal metadata required for scoped freshness; preserve deserialization of old plans, runs, and receipts without granting false freshness.
- Compute correct target-scoped identities from declared-complete inputs, transitive dependencies, and runner authority.
- Share a source projection or observation across targets when straightforward within the existing architecture.
- Fail conservatively when filesystem authority is unsupported, ambiguous, escaping, or cannot be collected.
- Add batching, indexing, caching, or a dedicated performance service only when the anonymized baseline demonstrates material repeated-walk cost.

## Scope Boundary

The inspected repository corpus contains no tracked symlinks or submodules. Do not build elaborate symlink or submodule projection logic. Minimal detection that returns unknown or blocked is sufficient. Do not make performance architecture a prerequisite for correctness.
acceptance_criteria:
- The separate freshness epoch uses ActionSpec.inputs plus the completeness policy from .4.1 and introduces no second path list.
- Versioned plan identity and additive journal metadata remain compatible with old plans, runs, and receipts without granting false freshness.
- Correct target-scoped fingerprints are deterministic across target ordering.
- Relevant direct inputs, transitive dependencies, and runner authority invalidate freshness while unrelated changes do not.
- Missing policy or unsupported, ambiguous, escaping, or failed authority returns unknown or blocked rather than fresh.
- Correctness does not depend on batching, indexing, caching, or a dedicated performance service.
- Source observation is shared when straightforward; further optimization requires anonymized roughly 4,000-file measurements demonstrating material repeated-walk cost.
- No elaborate symlink or submodule projection logic is introduced.

title: Let dev apps reuse serve-target launch authority
description:
## Outcome

A dev app can reference an authored serve target instead of duplicating launch command authority, while the existing dev supervisor retains all session semantics.

## Evidence

The inspected Jig configurations repeat every frontend identity and directory in dev configuration: one frontend across two dev apps, three across five, and five across six. This task removes that demonstrated authority duplication without generalizing dev sessions into repository runs.

## Scope

Add an optional serve-target reference to dev app source and resolved configuration. When present, resolve argv, cwd, and base environment from the referenced target. Keep host, port, proxy, readiness, restart, process supervision, and other session behavior in dev configuration. Define deterministic environment composition so dev-session values can augment the target base without creating a second base-command authority. Preserve update or recopy behavior and diagnostics for missing, incompatible, or conflicting references.

## Compatibility

Legacy inline dev app command, directory, and environment configuration remains readable and behaves unchanged. Repositories may migrate one dev app at a time.

## Product Boundary

The target reference reuses launch authority only. The existing dev supervisor launches and owns the process. Starting or stopping a dev session does not create a RunPlan, durable repository run, target result, receipt, or gate evidence. Do not add Vite, React, Node, Rust, Go, Electron, or other ecosystem-specific fields or inference to the repository contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- Optional serve-target references reuse target-owned argv, cwd, and base environment.
- Dev configuration remains authoritative for host, port, proxy, readiness, restart, and session lifecycle.
- Conflicting or invalid authority fails precisely before launch.
- Legacy inline and target-backed dev apps coexist and preserve existing inline behavior.
- Recopy preserves authored references and does not infer them.
- Dev sessions remain supervisor-owned and create no durable run, target result, receipt, or gate evidence.
- No Vite-specific or other ecosystem-specific contract semantics are introduced.

title: Persist exact Jig release pins across consumer updates
description:
## Outcome

Let downstream repositories commit an exact Jig release choice such as `0.3.0`, and retain that choice until an explicit upgrade. Users should not have to look up a source SHA to express a release pin. Keep the resolved immutable source identity as an internal lock detail for reproducibility.

## Problem and rationale

Current consumers can run `jig update --vcs-ref v0.3.0`, but the renderer stores only the resolved `_commit`. A later ordinary `jig update` follows the remote default branch; only `--recopy` retains the stored revision. In contract v4 and later, `jig_version` is accepted as legacy input but omitted/ignored for release selection. This loses the user's release intent and makes an apparently pinned consumer advance to development code.

A release selector must be distinct from the resolved lock identity: the version expresses the user's policy, while the source identity verifies exactly which code satisfies it. Package version output alone is insufficient because unreleased source can still report the same workspace version as a published release.

## Required behavior

- Add a supported, documented exact-SemVer release selector to committed consumer configuration. Keep its naming and validation consistent across the strict config parser, renderer, CLI, generated installer, and contract migration. Do not introduce a setting that is accepted but ignored.
- For release-pinned repositories, both ordinary `jig update` and `jig update --recopy` retain the selected release and resolved source identity. Re-rendering changed repository answers must not advance the runtime or template to another release or branch.
- Provide an explicit upgrade command, such as `jig update --version 0.3.1`, that resolves the release, checks compatibility, and changes the durable selection through the existing transaction boundaries. Reject ambiguous combinations with source/ref selectors rather than choosing an undocumented precedence.
- Released `init`/`adopt` flows should retain their selected release as durable intent. Development-branch tracking must be an explicit choice. Preserve explicit source-revision, local, embedded, and custom-template workflows; do not infer an official release pin from a local binary's version string or silently switch a fork to the official source.
- Make generated launchers and installers enforce the selected release and locked source identity, including cache reuse. A compatible contract/profile or matching `--version` string alone must not authorize an unrelated build. Existing explicit development overrides may remain available, but their use must be visible and must not rewrite or masquerade as the persisted release pin.
- Missing releases, invalid versions, conflicting pin/lock identity, moved release tags, and unavailable resolution must produce actionable errors without falling back to the default branch. Previously verified cached pinned runtimes should remain usable offline. Retain immutable-lock protections when release names are introduced.
- Migrate existing source-pinned repositories without moving their source or guessing a release. Preserve supported legacy contract v2/v3 behavior. On modern contracts, a recognized legacy `jig_version` must either be enforced through the supported migration or produce a clear migration diagnostic; never continue silently as though it selected a release.
- Keep requested release, resolved revision, actual runtime identity, and any explicit override understandable in human/JSON diagnostics and documentation. Update examples and generated guidance so ordinary updates and explicit upgrades have one consistent meaning.

## Entry points verified in the current repository

- `crates/jig/src/bootstrap/initial_template.rs`: released versus unreleased default template selection.
- `crates/jig/src/bootstrap/template_source.rs`: `prepare_update_template_source`, default-branch updates, and recopy revision handling.
- `crates/jig/src/bootstrap/answers/raw_answers.rs` and the strict context configuration parser: legacy version input and persisted answers.
- `scripts/install-jig.sh` and `templates/project/scripts/install-jig.sh.jinja`: legacy version cutoff, source stamps, cache selection, and `cargo install --rev`.
- `scripts/jig` and `templates/project/scripts/jig.jinja`: consumer launcher behavior and developer overrides.
- Generated contract/template snapshots, launcher parity tests, and runtime compatibility checks must remain synchronized.
- `docs/configuration.md`: current update/ref/recopy behavior and the accepted-key description of legacy `jig_version`.

Implement at the shared configuration, update-resolution, and runtime-installation boundaries so CLI, generated launchers, and MCP consumers share the same policy. A documentation-only change or a shell wrapper around `--vcs-ref` does not deliver the persistent pin.

## Verification

Use generic temporary repositories such as `ExampleProject` and a local Git template fixture with two release tags and a newer development head. Exercise real rendered configuration, update/recopy, generated launcher/installer selection, and recorded runtime identity. Do not depend on the existence of a future public `0.3.1` release or production credentials.

Cover an empty cache, a valid warm cache, an unrelated contract-compatible cache/PATH binary, an unreleased build with the same reported product version, offline reuse, tag movement, failed resolution, explicit upgrade, and explicit development override. Preserve custom template/source identity and authored commands. Include legacy contract migration cases and verify that failed upgrades leave the previous consumer state usable. Run relevant launcher/template parity, formatting, Clippy, contract, and backend checks through the development binary and repository harness.

## Dependencies and delivery boundary

No known prerequisite bead: the existing configuration, source-resolution, installer, and transaction machinery provide the implementation foundation. This task owns the complete consumer release-pin behavior; do not add unrelated backlog dependencies merely to create graph edges. It enables predictable release adoption and explicit upgrades for downstream consumers.

Create a task-local ExecPlan while implementing if needed, following repository policy. This bead is the delivery outcome, not a task to write or review a plan. Automatic upgrade scheduling, general SemVer ranges, a new distribution service, and redesigning runtime compatibility epochs are outside this request.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A downstream repository can commit an exact release selector such as 0.3.0 without manually finding a SHA; immutable resolved identity is retained internally.
2. Ordinary update, recopy, and launcher execution retain that release even when newer releases/development commits or unrelated compatible binaries are available.
3. An explicit version upgrade changes the selection and resolved identity coherently; failed resolution or incompatibility preserves usable prior state.
4. Installer/cache enforcement proves the selected release identity, including same-version unreleased builds, offline reuse, and moved-tag conflicts; there is no silent branch fallback.
5. Development tracking and runtime overrides are explicit and visible; custom/local/embedded/source-pinned consumers retain their intended source identity.
6. Legacy contract migration preserves supported behavior, and a recognized version setting is enforced or diagnosed rather than silently ignored.
7. Generated configuration/scripts, CLI/MCP behavior, human/JSON diagnostics, and documentation agree.
8. Generic end-to-end regressions exercise both persistence and actual runtime selection; relevant repository verification passes.

title: PR manager clears attempts for cancelled or unknown check observations
description:
## Current state

Audited against master `4ef2e902` on 2026-09-07. The classifier checks fail and pending counts but does not gate healthy cleanup on cancel/unknown buckets. jig-sh-ter describes the same defect.

## Implementation

Treat cancelled and unknown checks as indeterminate observations: preserve attempts, start no repair solely because of them, and expose pending/attention diagnostics. Success, skipped and neutral outcomes retain the intentional healthy policy. Keep mergeability uncertainty in jig-sh-lrk.

## Entry points

- `crates/jig/src/runtime/loops/pr_manager.rs`
- `crates/jig/src/runtime/loops/github.rs`
- `crates/jig/src/runtime/loops/pr_manager/attempt_clear_tests.rs`

## Validation

Run focused tests for the changed behavior, then build `cargo build -p jig-sh --bin jig` and use `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig work check --plan-id <implementation-plan>` for applicable repository gates. Finish backend changes with `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test`. Use generic isolated fixtures; no live services or credentials are required unless explicitly identified as an external prerequisite.

## Steps to Reproduce

Seed a repair attempt and classify otherwise healthy same-repository, non-draft snapshots with checks.summary.cancel=1 and unknown=1 separately. Run the tick from each snapshot and inspect attempt cleanup; both can currently fall through to Idle. Use fail/pending/pass/skipping controls.

## Acceptance Criteria

A bucket matrix proves cancel/unknown never clear attempts; pass/skipping can clear only when other health predicates pass. Fail starts eligible repair; pending preserves accounting. Cover mixed buckets and malformed counts conservatively.
acceptance_criteria: A bucket matrix proves cancel/unknown never clear attempts; pass/skipping can clear only when other health predicates pass. Fail starts eligible repair; pending preserves accounting. Cover mixed buckets and malformed counts conservatively.

title: Bound loop lease TTL before expiry arithmetic
description:
## Current state

Audited against master `4ef2e902` on 2026-09-07. validate_tuning only rejects zero TTL; expiry arithmetic still allows operationally unbounded leases.

## Implementation

Define a documented finite lease TTL ceiling shared by global/workflow config and CLI overrides. Use checked expiry arithmetic and reject out-of-range newly requested TTLs before state writes. Keep existing persisted records readable and provide explicit recovery guidance for oversized historical leases rather than silently shortening live ownership.

## Entry points

## Steps to Reproduce

Set lease_ttl_seconds to u64::MAX through config and a CLI override, resolve tuning, and inspect expiry using a controlled clock. Current validation accepts it and saturation can produce an effectively permanent lease.

## Acceptance Criteria

Zero, ceiling+1 and u64::MAX requests fail consistently through config/CLI; 1 and ceiling work. Near-overflow clocks cannot create saturated expiries. Rejection leaves state unchanged, and historical excessive leases have a documented safe recovery path.

title: Distinguish committed baseline changes from partial staging in work gates
description:
Older plan baselines can make ordinary unstaged edits fail legacy check-gate attestation as "partially staged", even when the index is identical to HEAD. Fix this false rejection while preserving rejection of genuinely divergent index/worktree content.

Confirmed reproduction

Reproduced with installed jig 0.3.0 using an isolated generic ExampleProject Git repository and a contract-v5 command-backed gate (example-source, paths = ["src/**"], command = "git diff --check"). The fixture exercised real Git and Jig commands; no source changes or check-result substitutions were made in the Jig repository.

1. Commit A contains src/lib.rs with VALUE = 1 plus the fixture config/manifest.
2. Commit B changes VALUE to 2; HEAD and index both equal B.
3. Open one plan with `jig work start --base <A>` and a control plan with `--base <B>`.
4. Change VALUE to 3 without staging. Confirm `git diff --cached --name-only` is empty.
5. `jig work check --plan-id <old-plan>` exits 1; applicability is unknown, with "Cannot attest partially staged gate input src/lib.rs". `work gates` is blocked.
6. Adding `--gate example-source` exits 0. The receipt has status=executed, exit_status=0, forced=true, applicability=unknown, and scope_error; `work gates` remains blocked. This is execution success, not attested gate evidence.
7. The HEAD-baseline control runs successfully and `work gates` reports passed on the same source/index state.
8. Stage VALUE = 3, then leave VALUE = 4 unstaged: the HEAD-baseline control correctly rejects actual partial staging. Preserve this protection.

Implementation surface

- crates/jig/src/git_receipts/scope.rs: gate_scope_snapshot_from_plan_change_inner / scope proof collection and ensure_no_partially_staged_paths (call near line 526; function near line 604).
- The guard intersects `git diff --cached <plan-baseline>` with index-to-worktree paths. Its first set includes changes already committed between the plan baseline and HEAD; it does not isolate actual HEAD-to-index staging. The relevant implementation is unchanged between v0.3.0 and inspected source HEAD a78ed49009f090a7350ee75b1db5487b96ba3bfa.
- crates/jig/src/runtime/work/checks.rs: classify_prepared_check deliberately allows forced execution with unknown applicability. Preserve that distinction and make the human-facing outcome explicit when a successful forced command remains unattested.
- crates/jig/src/runtime/work/gates.rs and gates/tail.rs: applicability, freshness, evidence and finish reporting must retain unknown/blocked when authority is unresolved.
- Existing regression anchor: crates/jig/src/git_receipts/tests_parts/part_02.rs::masked_staged_change_is_classified_and_fails_scope_proof.
- Runtime/CLI integration tests belong with crates/jig/src/runtime/tests/work.rs and work_parts; documentation in docs/configuration.md, Work Shape.

Scope and compatibility

Keep the plan baseline as the authority for changed-path applicability and evidence identity. Distinguish historical committed changes from actual partial staging using coherently captured Git identities; do not fix this by replacing every baseline with HEAD, ignoring the index, clearing scope errors, weakening the masked-staging guard, or editing historical receipts. Reuse current scope/evidence representations unless implementation proves a schema change necessary. This is a bounded correction to existing check-gate attestation, including legacy gates coexisting in v6/v7 repositories; it should not wait for the separate target-freshness epoch work in jig-sh-generic-monorepo-zac.4.2.

The file-budget evaluator itself is not the failing surface. A useful interim workflow is a work plan based on current HEAD with the older file-budget comparison supplied explicitly, but users must be able to choose an older work-plan baseline without this false partial-staging classification.
acceptance_criteria:
- A -> B committed change followed by an ordinary unstaged edit, with index == HEAD == B, is attestable for a plan based on A. Applicable changed paths and evidence identity still cover A-to-current.
- Include a committed-since-baseline path with no later edit so the fix cannot silently narrow applicability to HEAD-to-worktree.
- Preserve rejection of genuinely partially staged content and staged changes masked by restoring worktree bytes; retain existing staged-deletion/worktree-replacement safeguards. Cover HEAD-baseline and older-baseline cases, plus coherent fully staged edits.
- Add focused scope regression tests and an end-to-end work start --base / check / evidence / gates / finish fixture. Validate the shared behavior for legacy check gates, including coexistence with a supported modern contract.
- For genuinely unknown scope, forced commands may execute according to current compatibility behavior, but receipts and human output clearly distinguish execution success from usable gate evidence; work finish must remain blocked. Never promote unknown applicability merely because exit_status is zero.
- Relevant source/index/authority changes continue to invalidate evidence; failed or inconsistent Git collection remains unknown/blocked. Preserve bounded collection and existing journal compatibility.
- Update work-baseline/forced-check documentation with the distinction, using generic fixtures only. No downstream names or operational details in source, tests, docs or evidence.

title: Make Codex marketplace timeout regression robust under load
description:
## Current state

Audited against master `4ef2e902` on 2026-09-07. codex_support_probe_has_a_finite_owned_timeout still uses a 20ms busy-loop fixture.

## Implementation

Replace dependence on process startup within 20ms with explicit fixture readiness and a finite timeout oracle. Assert actual timeout classification and descendant cleanup, without broadening the production probe timeout.

## Entry points

- `crates/jig/src/runtime/agent.rs`

## Validation

Run focused tests for the changed behavior, then build `cargo build -p jig-sh --bin jig` and use `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig work check --plan-id <implementation-plan>` for applicable repository gates. Finish backend changes with `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test`. Use generic isolated fixtures; no live services or credentials are required unless explicitly identified as an external prerequisite.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run codex_support_probe_has_a_finite_owned_timeout in isolation and under bounded parallel process load. Its 20ms busy-loop fixture can classify unavailable instead of timeout. Capture actual fixture-start and child-exit state; a fresh failure is not claimed by this audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Accept SQLx 0.9 Cargo-subcommand version output in doctor
description:
## Observed behavior
Observed with Jig revision 4ef2e90280d053a6fc5a38477429dd3c0a61de44 and SQLx CLI 0.9.0. sqlx --version prints "sqlx-cli 0.9.0"; cargo sqlx --version (and cargo-sqlx sqlx --version) prints "sqlx-cli-sqlx 0.9.0". Doctor recognizes only the first product name, so the supported Cargo-subcommand configuration reports an invalid product name and jig setup fails even though the actual SQLx preparation check succeeds.

## Reproduction
Use an isolated ExampleProject with SQLx 0.9 and a trusted PATH installation of sqlx-cli 0.9.0 outside the repository. Configure the SQLx check as cargo sqlx prepare --check --workspace -- --workspace --all-targets. Compare the two version outputs, run scripts/jig doctor --json, and observe the sqlx_cli failure. A valid fixture database is only needed to separately demonstrate actual preparation success.

## Expected behavior and investigation
Accept the actual product/version output for each supported SqlxProbeStyle while retaining strict version validation. Entry point: probe_sqlx_cli_version in crates/jig/src/doctor_parts/part_03.rs. Do not loosen the separate rule that prevents doctor from probing untrusted checkout-contained executables. A working direct-SQLx invocation with explicit CARGO environment is a workaround, not a reason to reject the Cargo-subcommand form.
acceptance_criteria:
- Doctor accepts matching SQLx 0.9 direct and Cargo-subcommand product/version output.
- Incompatible minor versions, unrelated product names, malformed versions, and unexpected output remain rejected.
- Setup no longer fails solely because a valid Cargo-subcommand installation reports sqlx-cli-sqlx.
- Tests exercise both invocation styles with representative actual CLI output; preserve executable trust checks.
close_reason: Confirmed and fixed style-specific SQLx 0.9 product parsing. Direct and Cargo invocation/version fixtures pass; malformed output, incompatible minor versions, and checkout-contained probe executables remain rejected. All 35 focused SQLx doctor tests pass.

title: Consolidate shared authored-contract fixture foundations
description:
## Current state

Source audit at 9946d1b4 on 2026-09-11 confirmed this is remaining test consolidation, not missing production functionality. Runtime and MCP already share write_v6_evidence_fixture_repo in runtime/tests/common.rs. Bootstrap independently constructs authored models and repeats answer-file serialization/reload setup. The existing Go API + TypeScript web and TypeScript web + Markdown docs scenarios provide concrete topology foundations to reuse. The latter currently uses v6 command-backed file-loc actions; it is not a v7 native file-budget fixture.

The audit ran 96 selected tests successfully (2793 skipped); this is focused baseline evidence, not a full-suite or post-change result. Existing bootstrap tests with v6 in their names often reload authored answers without loading a version-pinned manifest.

## Release boundary and coordination

User-confirmed release contract (2026-09-11): 0.3.0 shipped v7; upcoming 0.4.0 will ship v8. A separate implementation is flattening the unreleased v8, v9 and v10 changes into v8. The audit's observed v10 constant is an intermediate source state, not a compatibility commitment.

Coordinate current-epoch fixture integration with that cutover: re-read the integrated epoch definitions and preserve the combined implemented behavior under v8. Inventory and shared setup extraction can proceed independently, but final current-epoch validation must use the flattened v8 implementation. Do not reimplement flattening, add v9/v10 compatibility obligations, or modify its production files. Keep explicitly pinned v6 compatibility and released-v7 native file-budget scenarios distinct from upcoming-v8 scenarios. A full topology-by-epoch matrix is not required; retain the existing compatibility cases and exercise both shared topologies at the upcoming epoch.

## Implementation

1. Inventory existing assertions and test cases before extraction, including tests reached through include! and child modules. Mark which assertions will move, which remain local, and which intentionally exercise different behavior. Record the actual manifest epoch separately from the test name; identify answer-only bootstrap tests separately.
2. Extract the narrow shared authored fixture data/writing mechanics for two named scenarios: (a) Go API at api plus TypeScript web at web, using the verify profile and test actions; (b) TypeScript web at web plus Markdown docs at docs, using the quality profile and file-loc actions. Preserve authored roots, IDs, bindings, profile choices and scenario-specific effects/inputs. Adapter labels are data; runtime execution uses local fixture commands, not ecosystem toolchains.
3. Reuse these definitions in bootstrap answer reload/render tests and runtime/MCP tests. Keep bootstrap RenderAnswers/RepositoryRenderModel handling local to bootstrap; keep repository loading, Git initialization, open-plan seeding, execution and worker waiting local to their test layers. Prefer a small cfg(test) module beside existing test support; do not make bootstrap production types accessible to runtime just to share fixtures. Reuse the existing runtime writer and TestRepoBuilder where appropriate rather than creating a competing all-purpose builder.
4. Share assertions only for identical observable contract invariants: component identity/root/adapter metadata, action target and runner/command bindings, and profile membership/defaults. Keep explicit expected values independent of the implementation under test. Layer-specific assertions remain visible in their tests: bootstrap authored ownership, command overrides, recopy and generated/declared distinctions; runtime selection, failure results, receipts and evidence; MCP wire schemas, queued/terminal states, approval, cancellation, registry and lease cleanup.
5. Preserve literal malformed/mismatched fixtures and source/authority mutation cases where the exact input is the test. Do not normalize away deliberately distinct config and manifest values or hide scenario changes behind a flag-heavy helper. Keep v6 command fixtures and v7 native file-budget/prepared-input fixtures explicitly versioned; upcoming-v8 fixtures use the flattened runner and freshness semantics.

Out of scope: adoption candidates (.1.3), source migration (.1.2), epoch flattening itself, dev serve-target integration (.6), new runtime capabilities/runners, repository-wide fixture cleanup, and a universal acceptance harness.

## Entry points

- crates/jig/src/test_env.rs and crates/jig/src/lib.rs: existing test-only support and module wiring.
- crates/jig/src/bootstrap/repository_model/tests.rs and tests/authored_workflows.rs: authored scenarios and reload/recopy assertions (the latter is included with include!).
- crates/jig/src/bootstrap/repository_model/tests/rust_file_loc.rs and tests/independent_checks.rs: authored/native ownership, reload helpers and prerequisite preservation.
- crates/jig/src/runtime/tests/common.rs: existing shared v6 writers, non-Rust file-loc topology, Git and plan setup.

title: Let dev apps reuse serve-target launch authority
description:
## Current state

Readiness audit at 9946d1b4 on 2026-09-11: argv and explicit-shell repository runners already exist; prerequisite .3.3 is closed. Dev apps still own inline commands independently. DevAppConfig, bootstrap DevApp, and AppRunSpec have no target reference/base-environment handoff. The separate dev spawn path does not currently use repository argv's literal-exec preparation. Existing tests preserve selected-only directory existence checking and explicit frontend/dev directory alignment.

141 selected tests passed across jig-sh and jig-dev-proxy during the audit (3268 skipped). This is baseline evidence, not validation of this feature or the separate epoch flattening.

## Release boundary

0.3.0 shipped v7; upcoming 0.4.0 ships v8. A separate implementation is flattening unreleased v8/v9/v10 behavior into v8. Deliver this optional dev binding in that flattened v8 contract. Reject serve_target on older manifests while preserving their inline dev behavior. Do not implement flattening, create a further epoch, or retain v9/v10 migration/compatibility promises. Reconcile constants and tests with the integrated cutover before final validation.

## Configuration and target eligibility

Add an optional serve_target string to [[dev.apps]], parsed as one exact TargetId. Example:

```toml
[[dev.apps]]
name = "web"
serve_target = "frontend:serve"
kind = "vite"
```

The target action need not literally be named serve; its intent must be Serve. App identity remains independent of component identity, so existing hostnames, selections and environment prefixes use the dev app name.

For target-backed entries, command and argv must be absent, including explicitly empty forms. Preserve field presence through validation where necessary. Do not change existing precedence/validation for configurations without serve_target. Do not resolve a legacy alias, profile, wildcard, action-wide selector or implicit default profile.

The selected target must have a valid literal Argv runner with nonempty NUL-free program and only literal argument positions. Reject all argument declarations, even optional/unused ones; no argument binding API is added. Reject command, shell and native runners. Reject action depends_on, explicit timeout_seconds, and non-default result_parser: dev will not execute prerequisites, impose repository action lifetimes, or interpret findings. Require Process and reject ReadOnly; Worktree and External declarations may accompany Process. This is explicit reuse of launch data by a trusted dev command, not execution/evidence of the repository action. Effects are descriptive here, not a dev sandbox or a new approval mechanism. Inputs, freshness policy, aliases and component dependency metadata remain repository metadata and neither schedule prerequisites nor produce dev freshness evidence.

## Working directory and frontend alignment

Resolve runner working_directory with existing repository semantics: repository-relative, default repository root when omitted, never implicitly component root. Convert that logical directory into the selected app's effective cwd. Preserve relative executable lookup against that cwd.

Allow optional [[dev.apps]].dir only as an assertion: normalize it and the logical runner cwd with existing portable repository-path rules and reject inequality. It cannot override cwd. For a same-name [[frontend_apps]] entry, compare its directory against the effective target directory; a target-backed app need not duplicate dir merely to pass alignment. Preserve existing rules for inline entries, legacy frontend fallback and discovery. Dependency readiness uses the resolved selected app directory and existing package-manager detection.

Separate pure configuration/target checks from selected-path filesystem checks. Config syntax, launch-form conflicts, reference existence/eligibility and logical frontend alignment are checked without requiring unrelated directories to exist. Apply --app/discovery selection, then canonicalize/check selected cwd existence, directory type and repository containment before any launch side effect. The existing RepositoryCatalog::from_context eagerly checks every action working_directory; do not call it indiscriminately and regress selected-only dev behavior. Reuse existing structural validation through a narrow separation from filesystem checks; keep normal repository execution's validation unchanged.

## Environment contract

No new user-facing [[dev.apps]].environment field. The target runner's environment is the sole authored overlay for target-backed apps. Carry it in an ephemeral resolved AppRunSpec field with an empty default for existing constructors.

Composition is inherited process environment, then target environment, then existing supervisor controls. Reuse runner environment validation. Preserve inherited OsString values, including non-UTF8 values; do not mutate parent-process environment or clear ordinary caller variables. Target PATH affects executable lookup; empty values are literal values, not deletion instructions.

Reject target environment declarations for HOST, PORT, ASTRO_DEV_BACKGROUND, __VITE_ADDITIONAL_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS, and keys matching the existing managed JIG_DEV_<APP>_{HOST,PORT,ORIGIN,URL} predicate. Reject even an apparently matching value because ports and selection can change. Do not reserve all JIG_DEV_* keys indiscriminately. Errors identify the app, target and conflicting key, without printing its value.

Continue stripping stale inherited managed coordinates before overlaying current selection coordinates. Preserve generated-npm detection and its narrow routing/dependency-class environment exclusions; apply that filter to the effective child environment, including newly supplied target keys. Custom commands keep the existing project-owned environment behavior. Do not persist resolved environment values in status, dev-session state, logs or debug rendering.

## Literal execution and supervisor boundary

Resolve launch authority in crates/jig, not jig-dev-proxy or jig-contract. Reload the current config/manifest once at dev launch resolution, preserving existing source/manifest equality checks, then use that invocation's resolved launch snapshot. Do not add a live target watcher, re-resolution loop or a durable RunPlan. Subsequent dev launches resolve the then-current authored configuration.

Pass only program/argv, resolved cwd, base environment and existing dev metadata to the supervisor. The lower crate must not learn TargetId, RepositoryCatalog, plans, receipts or gates. Preserve target-backed literal execution by narrowly sharing the existing no-implicit-shell-fallback preparation below both consumers (jig-owned-process is the existing common dependency). Share process preparation only; do not replace dev's specialized supervisor with the repository runner or change its identity/cleanup rules. Retain a distinction for target-backed literal execution so historical inline shell and argv behavior is not silently changed. Apply the guard after final argv, cwd, environment and process-group hooks are installed; its execve hook must not bypass group setup or freeze an incomplete environment.

The target supplies base argv; existing supervisor framework behavior may append validated Vite host/port/strict-port arguments and inject framework environment controls. Document this explicitly. Preserve --no-proxy, host/port assignment, dependency preflight, readiness/listener ownership, route publication, cancellation, stop/replace and cleanup. No new auto-restart mechanism is part of this task.

Validate every selected launch's static configuration before invoking dependency preflight, replacing/claiming a session, starting the proxy or starting any selected app. Port allocation/races and actual OS spawn failures remain supervisor-owned runtime failures with existing cleanup; do not promise all OS launches succeed atomically or pre-run executables to probe them.

## Integration scope

- crates/jig/src/context.rs, context/validation.rs and context/loading.rs: config presence, epoch checks and source authority.
- crates/jig/src/dev_proxy.rs and dev_proxy/commands/dev.rs: resolution, selection, frontend checks and launch handoff.
- crates/jig/src/repository.rs, repository/runners.rs and repository_path.rs: reuse structural runner/path validation without eager unrelated cwd checks.
- crates/jig/src/repository/runners/literal_exec.rs and crates/jig-owned-process/src/: narrow shared process preparation, only if needed; preserve existing repository tests.
- crates/jig-dev-proxy/src/types.rs, lib.rs, processes.rs and processes/frameworks.rs: ephemeral base environment, literal mode and existing supervisor controls.
- crates/jig/src/bootstrap_parts/part_01.rs, bootstrap/answers/dev.rs, bootstrap/answers/raw_answers.rs and templates/project/.jig.toml.jinja: preserve the authored binding through answer resolution, rendering and recopy. Inspect any generated template mirrors via the repository's established mechanism.
- crates/jig/src/info.rs, docs/configuration.md and docs/public-contract.md: truthful authored reference output, example, launch-only semantics and v8 availability.

Out of scope: automatic conversion of inline/generated apps, automatic creation of serve actions, dependency execution, parameterized/native/shell target reuse, new repository execution/state/effect policy, epoch flattening, and supervisor redesign. Do not widen production visibility merely to move data across the wrong boundary.

## Validation

Use generic temporary repositories and local helper executables; no live services, credentials, package installation, privileged ports, trust changes or user proxy state. Capture focused before/after results. Audit baseline:

```sh
cargo nextest run --offline -p jig-sh -p jig-dev-proxy --lib -P local -E '(package(jig-sh) & (test(dev_proxy::tests) | test(context::validation) | test(bootstrap::answers::dev::tests) | test(repository::runners))) | (package(jig-dev-proxy) & (test(lib::tests) | test(processes::tests)))' --status-level fail --final-status-level fail
```

This filter is not sufficient post-change validation. Add focused feature cases, target literal-runner regressions, bootstrap render/recopy/frontend tests, shared process tests if moved, and dev_lifecycle/dev_sigint coverage. Include mixed-app invalid-before-spawn markers and before/after .agent/state byte/existence assertions for launch/stop/replace. Assert loaded v7 and flattened-v8 manifests explicitly; verify --no-default-features build compatibility.

Follow the repository structured-work workflow. Build cargo build -p jig-sh --bin jig and use JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig work check --plan-id <implementation-plan>; inspect gates/evidence/receipts and finish backend work with JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test. Review the diff for contract drift, missing generated/config/info updates, fixture hygiene, file-budget policy and changes to inline behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In the flattened upcoming-v8 contract, [[dev.apps]].serve_target accepts one exact component:action identity whose authored action has intent=serve and a literal argv runner. The app name is independent of the component/action names. Target-backed and existing inline apps coexist; no generated inline app is automatically converted.
2. Reject malformed/missing/ambiguous references, aliases/profiles/wildcards, non-serve actions, command/shell/native runners, any argument declaration or argument binding, nonempty action depends_on, explicit action timeout_seconds, non-default result_parser, missing process effect, and read_only effects. Accept worktree/external effect declarations alongside process as described in the launch-only contract; no action effect enforcement or approval workflow is implied.
3. serve_target cannot coexist with command or argv, including explicitly supplied empty fields. Omitted target cwd means repository root. An optional app dir is an equality assertion against the normalized repository-relative target cwd, never an override. Matching frontend metadata must agree with that effective directory. Selected cwd paths must exist, be directories, and resolve inside the repository; an unselected app's missing directory must not block a valid selection.
4. Resolve and validate all selected launches before starting any app or replacing an existing session. A statically invalid selected launch must not execute a sibling marker command, run dependency preflight, claim/replace a session, or start a proxy. Existing runtime failures such as port races retain ordinary cleanup behavior; this is not an atomic OS-spawn guarantee.
5. Child environment inherits the caller and overlays target environment, then existing supervisor-owned controls. Reject target declarations for HOST, PORT, ASTRO_DEV_BACKGROUND, __VITE_ADDITIONAL_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS, and the existing managed JIG_DEV_<APP>_{HOST,PORT,ORIGIN,URL} key pattern. Remove stale inherited coordinates, preserve ordinary inherited variables and non-UTF8 values, and preserve narrow generated-npm filtering across both inherited and target-supplied keys. No separate dev-app environment override configuration is added.
6. Target-backed launches preserve literal program/argument bytes, declared PATH lookup, relative executable/cwd semantics, and rejection of executable text with ENOEXEC instead of implicit shell fallback. Preserve existing explicit inline shell behavior and Vite flag validation/injection. Shared literal-exec preparation runs after final cwd/environment/group-hook setup; specialized dev process ownership and cleanup remain intact.
7. Bootstrap answer parsing, normalization, validation, generation and recopy preserve serve_target and optional dir assertions. jig info reports the authored reference without flattening it into argv or exposing the resolved environment. v6/v7 inline fixtures retain their behavior, and serve_target is rejected below v8. No v9/v10 compatibility obligation or new contract epoch is introduced.
8. The Jig CLI resolves repository authority into a launch-only spec. jig-dev-proxy receives no target/catalog/RunPlan objects and gains no dependency on Jig repository runtime or state. Launch/stop/replace neither append nor create .agent/state run, receipt or gate evidence; existing machine-local dev-session/route state remains allowed and does not persist target environment values.
9. Tests cover mixed launch forms, exact eligibility/errors, environment collisions, root/default/custom cwd and symlink escapes, selected versus unselected paths, frontend alignment, literal execution/PATH, recopy and diagnostics, and existing no-proxy, readiness, stop/replace and process-tree cleanup behavior. All relevant gates pass with a freshly built dev binary; finish with JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test. Include the no-dev-proxy build and checks for any shared process primitive moved.
