title: Make LOC enforcement a template-owned repository action
description:
## Outcome

LOC limits become repository quality policy rather than Jig product policy. Rust templates still provide the existing LOC check by default, but the check is an ordinary command-backed repository action with the same planning, supervision, gate, and receipt behavior available to any language.

## Product Decision

Jig owns action selection, affected planning, dependency ordering, execution supervision, result parsing, durable evidence, and gates. A repository owns which files count as source, how lines are counted, thresholds, generated-file handling, exceptions, and legacy grandfathering. LOC does not protect a Jig correctness, security, persistence, or compatibility invariant, so it does not justify a native runtime branch.

A template may provide opinionated defaults. That is template policy, not a contract concept: repositories may replace or remove the action, and another language may add its own command-backed LOC action without changing Jig core. Repository ownership includes lifecycle authority: update and recopy must preserve an authored replacement, removal, alias choice, and profile membership instead of silently restoring the template default.

## Scope

First make the managed Rust checker self-contained while preserving the behavior currently implemented by `jig check rust-file-loc`. Then remove the dedicated CLI, command DTOs, dispatch, policy implementation, and native tests. Keep the generated Rust action and optional `jig.rust_file_loc` compatibility alias as ordinary declared command authority only. Route v6 automation through the resolved action/profile and prove an authored non-Rust LOC action uses the same generic execution and evidence path.

Update current source dogfooding, release/fixture invocations, documentation, managed templates, embedded snapshots, and contract compatibility coverage. Receipt and evidence updates apply to newly emitted records through the generic action path; historical `.agent/state/*.jsonl` remains truthful append-only memory and must not be rewritten. The existing Jig contract-v6 migration must consume this boundary rather than preserving the historical native policy.

## Compatibility

Perform the cutover in dependency order: publish the self-contained managed checker before deleting native behavior. Generated repositories are source-revision pinned, so historical repositories continue using the runtime matching their historical wrapper; update/recopy publishes the new checker and binding together. The current runtime must still load supported older contracts and execute LOC when it is declared as an ordinary command-backed tool. Do not retain native LOC semantics solely as an undocumented fallback for obsolete wrapper contents.

## Non-Goals

Do not introduce a generic LOC schema, threshold DSL, `FileLocPolicy` runtime type, language registry branch, native cross-language checker, mandatory TypeScript policy, new action runner, second planner, or new evidence format. Do not change the generic action-execution design owned by the repository-action feature.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh Rust templates include their LOC policy as an ordinary command-backed repository action in the default verification profile.
- Jig core exposes no native Rust LOC policy implementation or dedicated Rust LOC command semantics.
- The current Rust thresholds, baseline behavior, and exception rules remain available through the template-owned checker.
- A non-Rust component can author and run an equivalent LOC action without a Jig schema, registry, CLI, or runtime change.
- Supported older contract shapes continue to execute a declared LOC command tool without native dispatch.
- CI, docs, generated snapshots, and newly emitted work evidence and receipts reflect the repository-action ownership boundary; historical append-only state is not rewritten.
- No generic LOC DSL, native cross-language LOC engine, universal thresholds, or TypeScript LOC default is introduced.
- After a repository replaces or removes the template LOC action, compatibility alias, or default-profile membership, update and recopy preserve that authored authority and do not recreate omitted defaults.
close_reason: Completed

title: Make the managed Rust LOC checker self-contained
description:
## Outcome

The managed Rust LOC checker becomes the complete implementation of the Rust template's opinionated source-size policy. It no longer delegates policy to Jig core, so it can serve as the command implementation behind an ordinary repository action and legacy command alias.

## Why This Comes First

Deleting native policy before publishing a replacement would break the current source repository, generated CI, release validation, rendered-repository fixtures, and older command-backed contracts. This task establishes behavioral equivalence at the repository boundary before the runtime surface is removed.

## Scope

Move the characterized behavior from `crates/jig/src/policy.rs` into the managed checker source and its embedded snapshot. Preserve the current physical-line semantics and thresholds: information above 400, soft warnings above 500 and 600, hard failure above 800, and absolute failure above 1000. Preserve non-increasing legacy files above hard or absolute thresholds, rename-aware previous counts, `agentic-loc-exception:` and `@generated` markers within the first 40 lines, and the distinction between errors, warnings, and informational output.

Give the checker a direct, testable invocation contract covering the generated positional default-branch form plus `--changed-against REF`, `--staged`, and `--all`. Exactly one mode is effective. The default-branch form resolves the remote merge base when available and retains the documented local/empty-tree fallbacks. Use NUL-delimited Git authority throughout candidate and rename discovery; do not regress paths merely because shell implementation is convenient.

Keep this implementation Rust-template-specific: Rust roots, `*.rs`, thresholds, and annotations belong in the checker. Do not create Jig configuration fields or a reusable cross-language LOC library. The generated contract-v6 `rust-file-loc` action continues to point at this command, and the current source repository can continue declaring `jig.rust_file_loc` as a command-backed compatibility tool.

## Validation Ownership

Add focused checker tests for every mode and policy band, new and deleted files, renamed oversized legacy files, annotated and generated files, invalid mode combinations, missing refs, and unusual valid filenames. Update rendered-repository smoke coverage to demonstrate the checker runs without native LOC support. Keep fixtures unmistakably generic.

## Root And Counting Compatibility

Preserve the configured Rust source-root authority currently supplied by `rust_crate_roots`; do not silently hard-code `crates`. The managed template must safely represent zero, one, or multiple valid repository-relative roots, including `.`. To preserve current Git pathspec behavior, zero configured roots means repository-wide Rust candidate selection rather than an empty candidate set. Update or recopy must refresh generated default root authority without overriding a repository-authored replacement action.

Match the current line-count boundary exactly: an empty file has zero lines, each non-empty final segment counts even without a trailing newline, and LF or CRLF line endings produce the same line count. Validate these cases at the exact 400, 500, 600, 800, and 1000 boundaries so a shell implementation cannot substitute newline counting with different behavior.

## Shell Portability

The managed checker must run on the stock macOS Bash 3.2 surface as well as supported newer Bash versions. Do not use associative arrays, `mapfile` or `readarray`, empty-array expansions that fail under `set -u`, or other post-3.2 syntax. Preserve NUL-delimited Git parsing with Bash 3.2-compatible primitives and cover the generated script with a macOS or equivalent Bash 3.2 portability smoke test.
acceptance_criteria:
- The managed checker performs LOC enforcement without invoking a native `jig check rust-file-loc` implementation.
- Positional default-branch, `--changed-against`, `--staged`, and `--all` modes have one documented, fail-closed selection contract.
- The existing 400/500/600/800/1000 informational, soft, hard, and absolute thresholds are preserved.
- Legacy non-growth above hard/absolute limits, rename baselines, first-40-line exception markers, generated markers, deletions, and new files retain characterized behavior.
- Candidate and rename handling is safe for valid Git path bytes supported by the existing harness, including whitespace and line breaks, and does not parse line-delimited Git filenames.
- Errors produce nonzero status; warnings and informational findings remain successful and identify the affected repository-relative file.
- The managed template source and embedded snapshot stay identical, and focused tests cover every policy branch and invocation mode.
- The checker uses only dependencies guaranteed by supported generated Rust repositories on Linux and macOS.
- The generated checker preserves configured Rust source-root authority without hard-coding `crates`: zero roots retain repository-wide Rust candidate selection, while one or multiple valid roots, including `.`, constrain Git pathspecs as today; focused tests cover each case plus update or recopy refresh.
- Line counting preserves the characterized empty-file, LF, CRLF, trailing-newline, and unterminated-final-line behavior at every exact threshold boundary.
- The generated checker executes on stock macOS Bash 3.2 and supported newer Bash versions without post-3.2 syntax; portability coverage exercises NUL-delimited candidates and the zero-root case under `set -u`.
close_reason: Completed

title: Remove native Rust LOC policy and use repository actions end to end
description:
## Outcome

Jig runtime and CLI no longer know how to count Rust lines or enforce Rust-specific size policy. Every active LOC check, including the Rust template default, executes as repository-declared command authority through the ordinary contract-v6 action path.

## Dependency

This task begins only after the managed checker is self-contained and behaviorally characterized. The deletion must not create a window where generated repositories or the Jig source tree have no functioning LOC gate.

## Core Removal

Delete the dedicated `rust-file-loc` Clap subcommand and options, command/request/input DTOs, conversion and runtime dispatch arms, `PolicyCheckCommand` branch, compiled LOC constants and implementation, Rust-only candidate/rename helpers that become unused, CLI/tool-definition constants, moved-command hints, and native policy unit tests. Remove the name from strict launcher subcommand metadata so contract-v6 parsing can treat `rust-file-loc` as an external action selector.

Do not replace the removed code with a generic native LOC abstraction. The ordinary action runner, input globs, profiles, result parsing, receipts, and work evidence are the complete Jig product surface.

## End-to-End Cutover

Update source and generated command bindings, release validation, rendered-repository scripts, workflow templates, bootstrap previews, help text, documentation, and embedded snapshots. On contract v6, `jig check rust-file-loc` is selector syntax for the authored action; it is no longer a special command and accepts no LOC-specific flags. Direct policy-mode validation uses `scripts/check-rust-file-loc.sh`.

Generated v6 repository-policy CI should invoke the resolved selector or verification profile so the template default exercises the same action path as any custom language check. During the source repository's pre-v6 interval, its declared `jig.rust_file_loc` command tool may continue to call the self-contained checker; the existing v6 dogfood bead will complete that source cutover after this task.

## Compatibility

Keep supported contract epochs readable and keep normal command-backed tool execution intact. An alias named `jig.rust_file_loc` may remain in a generated or authored manifest, but it is data: the runtime resolves its command like any other alias. Add coverage for a supported older contract whose LOC command is self-contained and verify there is no recursion or native fallback. Historical generated repositories remain bound to their configured source revision; update/recopy publishes the new managed checker before a repository moves to the source revision containing this deletion. For an authored contract-v6 repository, recopy must preserve an exact replacement or removal of the LOC action, its compatibility alias, and its profile membership; template defaults apply only while the generated model remains unmodified.

## Stack-Neutral Proof

Add a lightweight contract-v6 fixture with a non-Rust component, ordinary source files, and a repository-authored `file-loc` command action. Prove exact and action-wide selector resolution, affected input selection, supervised failure, and newly emitted receipts and required evidence use the generic machinery without a language registry edit. Preserve historical append-only receipts and journals unchanged. The fixture checker may be deliberately small; it proves ownership and execution parity, not a TypeScript policy recommendation.

## Documentation Boundary

Document LOC as an example of template-provided repository policy. State that templates may provide defaults, repositories own semantics, and new languages add ordinary actions. Remove statements classifying Rust LOC as runtime-owned or native. Keep fixture identifiers generic and do not introduce downstream project details.
acceptance_criteria:
- `CheckRustFileLocOpts`, `RustFileLocRequest`, `RustFileLocInput`, native dispatch variants, compiled thresholds, Rust candidate helpers, and dedicated policy tests are absent from Jig core.
- Contract v6 resolves `jig check rust-file-loc` as the ordinary authored action selector; LOC-specific mode flags belong only to the checker command.
- Generated v6 CI and work verification execute the resolved Rust LOC action/profile instead of bypassing it or invoking native policy.
- `jig.rust_file_loc`, when retained for compatibility, is only a manifest-declared command alias and has no feature-registry or native runtime semantics.
- Supported pre-v6 contract fixtures execute a self-contained command-backed LOC tool without recursion or native fallback.
- An authored non-Rust component LOC action participates in selection, affected planning, supervision, receipts, and evidence using only existing generic contracts.
- Help, launcher metadata, docs, release checks, fixture scripts, embedded snapshots, and generated workflows contain no stale native-LOC instructions.
- Focused tests plus `cargo test -p jig-sh` and a freshly built `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test` pass.
- No generic LOC engine, LOC schema, threshold configuration, or TypeScript LOC default is added.
- Recopy and update coverage proves that authored replacement or removal of the LOC action, `jig.rust_file_loc` alias, and verification-profile membership survives without regeneration of omitted defaults.
- Newly emitted LOC receipts and work evidence identify the generic repository action path, while existing `.agent/state/*.jsonl` history remains unchanged and readable.
close_reason: Completed

title: Make file budgets a universal repository capability
description:
## Outcome

Jig supplies one language-neutral reviewability-budget engine while each repository owns strict checked-in policy. Physical lines and exact bytes use a per-metric no-growth debt ratchet across explicit Git comparison authority.

## Architecture

title: Align generated bootstrap entrypoints and explicit database setup
description:
## Problem
In the generated Rust/PostgreSQL + React scaffold at revision 4ef2e90280d053a6fc5a38477429dd3c0a61de44, the root package bootstrap script invokes only scripts/check-webapps.sh bootstrap, while scripts/jig bootstrap fetches Rust dependencies, installs frontend dependencies, requires DATABASE_URL, and runs --bootstrap-database. The generated README describes the package command as Jig dependency bootstrap and says bootstrap does not require a database. The differently scoped entrypoints share the same name and make first-use behavior difficult to predict.

## Requested improvement
Establish one documented dependency-bootstrap contract and a separately named database initialization operation. Make package scripts, Jig configuration, setup orchestration, generated README, and fresh-checkout instructions agree. The preferred behavior is dependency bootstrap without database/provider credentials, followed by explicit database setup using the existing role's authority. Preserve project-owned command overrides on later update/recopy; assess whether Go/PostgreSQL scaffolds share the same ambiguity rather than changing them blindly.

## Reproduction and entry points
Generate an isolated ExampleProject with Rust, PostgreSQL, React, and Bun. Compare root package.json bootstrap with .jig.toml repo_bootstrap_command, then inspect behavior without DATABASE_URL or .env. Relevant sources: crates/jig/src/bootstrap/scaffold/frontend/workspace.rs, templates/scaffolds/rust-react/frontend/workspace/package.json.jinja, templates/scaffolds/rust-react/frontend/workspace/README.md.jinja, and setup orchestration. Use generic fixtures and no real credentials.
acceptance_criteria:
- Package and Jig bootstrap entrypoints implement the same documented dependency behavior, or are explicitly named and documented when intentionally different.
- Dependency bootstrap succeeds without database credentials and does not initialize a database.
- Explicit database setup reports missing credentials or role/database permissions clearly and never creates roles or silently broadens permissions.
- Generated setup instructions work end to end and update/recopy preserves authored commands.
- Regression coverage exercises generated scripts and configuration, not just matching documentation strings.
close_reason: Generated package and Jig bootstrap now share credential-free dependency setup; Rust and Go database initialization is explicit via scripts/setup-database.sh and database:setup. Instructions, setup phases, ownership preservation, and permission errors align. Generated entrypoint/update/recopy regressions, 36 scaffold tests, nested-Go script test, and 3 setup tests pass. Real Cargo/Bun bootstrap succeeded without database configuration; disposable PostgreSQL confirmed permission rejection without role changes and exactly-once migration across repeated setup with a pre-created database.

title: Decide and enforce an aggregate GitHub PR snapshot budget
description: Out-of-scope open question from the feat/jig-loop-iteration comprehensive review. title: PR manager treats UNKNOWN mergeability as healthy idle state
description:
## Current state

## Implementation

Model indeterminate mergeability explicitly. Preserve attempt accounting and report pending observation without launching a repair solely for UNKNOWN. Apply the same conservative rule to missing or malformed mergeability; keep real conflicts actionable and known-clean states eligible for cleanup.

## Entry points

- `crates/jig/src/runtime/loops/pr_manager.rs`
- `crates/jig/src/runtime/loops/pr_manager/attempt_clear_tests.rs`

## Steps to Reproduce

## Acceptance Criteria

Repeated UNKNOWN/missing/malformed observations neither consume nor clear attempts. A later known clean result may clear; a known conflict may repair. Cover interaction with failing, cancelled and pending checks.

title: Report repository profile results in the work-check human summary
description:
## Observed behavior
Observed with Jig revision 4ef2e90280d053a6fc5a38477429dd3c0a61de44. An evidence-only verify gate ran twelve repository targets successfully. The final human summary nevertheless reported "Work check: no checks configured", "Checks: 0", and a next step to configure checks. The JSON result contained ok=true, checks=[], a completed run, twelve results, and no failed_targets; work gates/evidence confirmed fresh passing receipts.

## Reproduction
Create an isolated ExampleProject with repository action targets, a verify profile, and a work gate using kind="evidence", profile="verify", conclusion="success". Start a plan and run work check in human and JSON modes. Use deterministic harmless fixture commands and inspect both the user summary and recorded target evidence.

## Expected behavior and investigation
Summarize executed repository targets as well as legacy tool checks. An empty legacy checks array does not mean no checks ran. Include the actual target outcomes and relevant run/receipt identity, and suggest inspecting gates after success. Entry points: crates/jig/src/cli/output/work.rs and crates/jig/src/cli/output_tests/evidence.rs. Existing fixture expectations should be checked against the real current execution payload rather than assuming a nested run.targets shape. Keep execution and receipt truth unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- Evidence-only profile success produces a passing human summary with the correct target count and outcomes.
- Evidence-only failure/cancellation cannot be reported as success or no checks configured.
- Mixed legacy/profile runs, reused evidence, and a genuinely empty configuration have distinct accurate summaries.
- A regression formats the actual execution-result shape from a generic integration fixture, including top-level results where emitted.
close_reason: Human work-check output now summarizes durable target outcomes and top-level compatibility results, run and receipt identity, mixed legacy/profile checks, and failure/incomplete states. Enabled orphaned evidence regressions and fixed profile evidence labels; all 62 CLI output tests pass, including actual profile execution.

title: Preserve explicit Rust guide roots across harness updates
description:
## Observed behavior
Observed with Jig revision 4ef2e90280d053a6fc5a38477429dd3c0a61de44 in a generated Rust/PostgreSQL + React workspace. A harness update replaced explicit rust_crate_roots = ["apps", "crates"] with ["."], derived from the root backend repository component. The affected guide validator then treated web/AGENTS.md as Rust, demanded Rust entrypoints/sections, and failed to validate seven real backend guides. Restoring the explicit roots restored correct validation.

## Reproduction
Create an isolated ExampleProject workspace with a root Cargo workspace, packages beneath apps/ and crates/, a web frontend with its own non-Rust AGENTS.md, and valid backend guides. Configure the backend repository component at root "." and explicit guide roots ["apps", "crates"]. Run jig update against the affected revision, inspect .jig.toml, then run scripts/jig check agent-guides --json. Compare discovered guides before and after update.

## Expected behavior and investigation
Repository action roots and guide discovery roots must not be conflated. Preserve explicit supported guide roots across update/recopy, or derive equivalent backend package coverage without classifying frontend guides as Rust. Inspect crates/jig/src/bootstrap/answers/raw_answers.rs and crates/jig/src/policy/agent_map.rs. Latest guide discovery has evolved since the observed revision; verify remaining behavior before implementing and cover both the update and validator boundaries. Do not solve this by requiring Rust sections in frontend guides or suppressing guide validation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Update and recopy preserve correct guide coverage for a root Rust workspace with nested apps/crates and a frontend.
- Every intended backend guide is validated; web and documentation guides are not classified as Rust.
- An intentionally invalid nested backend guide still fails after update.
- An integration regression exercises actual rendered configuration and guide discovery using generic temporary fixtures.
close_reason: Preserved explicit guide discovery roots independently of component roots and file-budget actions. Update and recopy regressions reproduce the prior overwrite and now retain backend coverage, exclude web/docs, and reject an invalid nested guide; 27 repository-model tests pass.

title: Support targeted retries with current profile evidence
description:

## Implementation

Select latest original target receipts within the same work plan, preserving configuration/input/worktree/time validity and newer failures/unknown evidence. Compose profile evidence without inventing one run ID. Default checks reuse current independent passes and execute repairs in dependency order. Preserve selected receipts during archive. Forward ToolRequest plan identity via its existing accessor into native planning. Inspect the existing exploratory branch mentioned in notes before reusing it; it is not a validated baseline. This is receipt selection under existing conservative freshness, not the later target-scoped freshness epoch.

title: Make existing Go and frontend repository adoption accurate
description:
An installed jig 0.3.0 preview against a generic ExampleProject containing backend/go.mod and backend/migrations/001_init.sql reports SQLx, no Rust workspace, and generates clippy and sqlx gates. The migration can be a Goose migration; no Cargo.toml or .sqlx is needed for this false positive. Separately, a Vite frontend with dev, lint, typecheck, build, and test scripts disappears from the detected stack when build:bundle and test:coverage are absent.

Outcome: adoption identifies the existing Go backend and frontend, distinguishes detected components from checks ready to generate, and never infers Rust SQLx from generic SQL migration filenames. Preserve authored component/action/profile authority and repository-owned source, scripts, workflows, and guides. Detection belongs at bootstrap; do not add language-specific semantics to the generic runtime contract.

Implementation graph: jig-sh-so4.1 -> jig-sh-so4.3; jig-sh-so4.3 + jig-sh-so4.4 + jig-sh-so4.2 -> jig-sh-so4.5. SQLx and frontend fixes can ship independently. General candidate/exclusion policy shipped upstream in 6817728b and jig-sh-generic-monorepo-zac.1.3 is closed; reuse that implementation. The related edge records that foundation, not pending work.

Use only generic fixtures (ExampleProject, example.com/ExampleProject). Never copy downstream names, source, paths, or operational details into issues, tests, plans, or receipts. Planning scope is these five implementation tasks, not a new project or a contract redesign.

Upstream reconciliation (6817728b, 2026-09-08): the original reproduction above describes installed 0.3.0. Source now discovers Go/Node candidates, supports exact-root include/exclude decisions and preserves authored models. Root Go modules are accepted and select Go rendering; selected nested Go modules currently become components without actions. SQLx selection is disabled without an accepted root Rust component, but the raw migration heuristic and pre-selection warnings remain. Frontend readiness still controls framework/stack reporting. The five children are scoped to these remaining gaps; none claims to reimplement completed candidate infrastructure. Reconciliation was grounded in source and existing tests, not a rerun of the newly fetched runtime.
acceptance_criteria: All five children pass their acceptance criteria. Human and JSON previews agree with generated harness behavior. A Go plus Goose plus incompletely configured Vite fixture is identified truthfully; Go checks use the module root, clippy/SQLx are absent without supporting evidence, and frontend readiness gaps remain visible. Preview is non-mutating; write and recopy preserve authored ownership. Relevant configured gates and final scripts/jig check test pass using the freshly built dev binary.

title: Extend Go adoption candidates with workspace evidence and stack reporting
description:
Current state after upstream 6817728b: adopt_infer/components.rs discovers go.mod and accepts a valid root Go module; nested Go manifests appear as review-required candidates and can be explicitly included. It only checks for a nonempty module line, without Go/toolchain or go.work membership inference. adopt_infer.rs summary and adopt_infer/profile.rs detected_stack still omit Go. Extend this existing discovery and selection path; do not add another Go candidate system.

Implement Go discovery using adopt_infer/scan.rs, its bounded reads and existing traversal/exclusion rules. Record repository-relative module roots, go.mod module identity and declared Go/toolchain versions, go.work local use membership, sources, confidence, and diagnostics. Parse these files without running Go, downloading modules, or executing repository scripts. Root modules and a sole conventional backend/go.mod with production Go source are high-confidence candidates; raw incidental manifest hits under fixture/vendor/example trees are not automatic production authority. Invalid, ambiguous, out-of-root, or unreadable workspace members remain diagnostics, never silently promoted. Surface multiple modules and mixed Rust/Go candidates without picking one language for the entire repository.

Expose deterministic Go evidence in the human summary, JSON report, and stack label. Keep detection distinct from authored components and existing explicit answers. Reuse the shipped ComponentCandidate/Ecosystem/Disposition types and --include-component/--exclude-component interface from closed jig-sh-generic-monorepo-zac.1.3. Preserve review-required disposition for ambiguous manifests; any automatic inclusion of a sole conventional backend must be justified by additional production/workspace evidence, not its pathname alone. This task owns discovery/report tests, and hands accepted root/evidence data to jig-sh-so4.3.

Why: module-root and workspace evidence is required to choose valid command working directories; a scaffold preset or Rust fallback cannot supply it for an existing project. Entry points: adopt_infer.rs, adopt_infer/discovery.rs, adopt_infer/components.rs and components/{authority,workspace,tests}.rs, adopt_infer/selection.rs, adopt_infer/scan.rs, adopt_infer/profile.rs, and bootstrap/tests/basic/adoption_components.rs. Existing root-module and exact-root selection behavior is regression coverage, not new scope.

Validation: focused inference tests and final freshly built JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test. Runtime implementation must follow crates/jig/AGENTS.md and structured work/gate guidance in root AGENTS.md.

Valid candidates and rejection reasons appear consistently in deterministic human/JSON output. No subprocess Go execution or writes are needed for detection. Explicit authored component authority remains intact; no arbitrary module is selected in an ambiguous tree.

title: Require SQLx-specific evidence before enabling SQLx adoption
description:
Current state after upstream 6817728b: infer_sqlx in adopt_infer/rust_sqlx.rs still unconditionally enables SQLx for a numbered SQL migration. Initial adopt_infer/discovery.rs calls it before component selection. The new adopt_infer/selection.rs subsequently clears SQLx values/signals when there is no accepted root Rust component, so do not claim that current pure-Go final selection still necessarily generates a SQLx gate. Initial warnings can survive, and an accepted Rust root still does not prove that its generic migration files use SQLx. Fix the underlying evidence and reporting, retaining selection-aware scoping.

Separate migration-path discovery from database-tool identification. Generic numbered SQL files may provide candidate migration locations after SQLx is established; they must not enable it. Retain verified SQLx-specific evidence already supported (Cargo dependency, SQLx metadata, Rust sqlx::migrate! usage, actual cargo sqlx shell/CI invocation), including repositories with nested Cargo manifests. Keep existing bounded parser semantics and avoid treating unrelated mentions/comments as commands. In mixed Go/Rust repositories, associate migration candidates with the supported owner; never choose an unrelated Goose directory alphabetically. If ownership cannot be established, report ambiguity and require an explicit migration path before generating a misleading SQLx migration command. Do not let the existing synthesized migrations/ fallback erase that ambiguity; preserve its supported behavior when positive SQLx evidence exists and no migration candidates were found.

Preserve explicit --sqlx-enabled true/false and answers-file precedence, including the existing actionable rejection of explicit SQLx enablement for a Go-only model without a Rust owner. Explicit disable must be reflected by the effective review and generated gates even when detection found SQLx; evidence may remain visible as evidence. Existing authored SQLx configuration is not silently disabled by update/recopy. The current bug fix concerns inferred adoption defaults, not rewriting persisted contracts.

Why: filenames are shared across migration tools. Disabling SQLx whenever Go is present would also be wrong for mixed repositories. Inspect adopt_infer.rs apply_sqlx_inference/apply_to_answers/adoption_review, answers/input.rs, and existing SQLx inference tests when changing evidence and presentation. No longer blocks jig-sh-so4.3: upstream selection now clears inferred SQLx without an accepted root Rust component. This fix remains a prerequisite of combined acceptance in jig-sh-so4.5. Preserve the selected-component scan boundaries and cover both raw inference and final selection.

Validation: focused SQLx/adoption tests plus final freshly built JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test; use generic fixture names before receipt-producing commands.
acceptance_criteria: A SQL-only migration fixture and a Go+Goose fixture infer sqlx_enabled=false, no .sqlx-default warning, and no generated SQLx gate. Positive Cargo dependency, .sqlx metadata, macro and cargo-sqlx-command fixtures retain support. Explicit true/false overrides and authored update/recopy ownership are covered. Mixed-language multiple-migration fixtures select only justified SQLx paths or present an actionable ambiguity, never a guessed Goose path. Human effective review agrees with generated gates. Include an accepted plain Rust root with generic SQL migrations and no SQLx evidence, and verify pre-selection warnings cannot retain false SQLx attribution after final selection.

title: Generate Go checks for accepted nested modules and workspaces
description:
Current state after upstream 6817728b: adopt_infer/selection.rs selects Go compatibility defaults for an accepted root Go module. repository_model/adoption.rs::from_adoption generates backend actions for an accepted matching root backend. Other accepted Go candidates, including --include-component backend, receive a component with the go adapter and an instruction to add actions explicitly, but no Go actions. Root Go support therefore exists; remaining work is executable actions for accepted nested modules/workspaces and mixed layouts. Existing Go defaults are `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, and `go mod verify && go test -mod=readonly ./...`; bind their cwd to the owning module instead of assuming repository root.

Consume accepted Go inference through answer resolution and the existing authored repository component/action/profile rendering path. Preserve explicit answers and complete authored models; do not invent a new contract epoch, a repository-wide language restriction, or require a scaffold preset. A high-confidence sole backend module should be usable with plain jig adopt. Root modules, accepted multi-module workspaces, and mixed Rust/Go components need commands rooted at the corresponding component and no omitted accepted module. Use the shipped include/exclude selection controls. Preserve the current ability to write only accepted candidates while leaving ambiguous candidates visibly unconfigured; do not introduce a global write failure merely because an unrelated candidate remains review-required.

Generate Go format, static-analysis and test actions using existing Go adapter capabilities and project-owned command overrides where safely recognized; honor working directories, failure propagation and command quoting. Do not assume go test ./... from the repository root covers a nested module or every go.work member. Only include strict/locked checks when their existing contract is satisfied. Go-only adoption must not inherit clippy, Cargo bootstrap steps, Rust toolchain requirements, Rust crate guidance, or SQLx. Goose or pgx evidence alone does not prove sqlc use, PostgreSQL deployment setup, or a safe migration command: do not add those gates/services without specific evidence or explicit configuration.

Audit dependent rendering: .jig.toml, .agent/jig-contract.json, generated gates, root/nested agent guides and map, bootstrap/doctor expectations, scripts, and managed CI. Preserve source, go.mod versions, repository-owned scripts and workflows. Existing supported Rust and authored mixed-model behavior must remain compatible through update/recopy.

Entry points: bootstrap/adopt_infer/selection.rs; bootstrap/answers/adoption.rs, adoption_commands.rs and resolution.rs; bootstrap/repository_model/adoption.rs, adoption_refresh.rs and repository_model.rs; repository_model/tests/go_workflow.rs and tests/authored_workflows.rs; bootstrap/tests/basic/adoption_components.rs; templates/project; crates/jig-go/src/lib.rs. Reuse existing mechanisms rather than creating a parallel Go execution layer.

Why: users rely on adoption to author executable checks, not merely accurate labels. Depends on richer Go evidence in jig-sh-so4.1; unblocks integrated acceptance. SQLx evidence cleanup is independently tracked by jig-sh-so4.2, since upstream now disables inferred SQLx when no root Rust component was accepted. Run focused render/contract tests, inspect the complete diff, build cargo build -p jig-sh --bin jig, use JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig for structured configured work gates, and finish with scripts/jig check test.
acceptance_criteria: Generic root and nested Go fixtures produce a valid executable Go contract and appropriate guides/toolchain checks with no Rust/SQLx requirements. A working-directory-sensitive test proves nested commands execute at the module root and propagate failure, including a generic module directory containing spaces. go.work/multiple accepted modules have complete coverage or an explicit unresolved-selection diagnostic, never silent omission. Explicit wrappers and authored mixed-language contracts are preserved. No unnecessary Goose/sqlc/database gates appear. Preview/write/update/recopy retain ownership and supported Rust scaffold/adoption regressions pass.

title: Report detected frontend apps separately from CI readiness
description:
Problem: crates/jig/src/bootstrap/adopt_infer/frontend.rs requires lint, typecheck, build:bundle, and test:coverage before retaining a frontend app. A normal Vite package with dev, lint, typecheck, build, and test is dropped from the managed frontend list, so the stack says no frontend apps and ignores its package manager. Upstream 6817728b separately exposes package.json as a Node component candidate; reuse that record rather than claiming that all frontend discovery is absent or adding another candidate identity.

Separate a detected frontend candidate/profile from a frontend eligible for Jig's existing managed web checks. Use current package/workspace discovery, framework/dev evidence, provenance, and bounded parser behavior. Human and JSON preview must identify a Vite app at frontend/, its pnpm lockfile evidence when present, and explicitly list missing build:bundle/test:coverage as readiness gaps. Report detected count and configured-for-checks count separately so no review message denies the app exists. Prefer additive candidate/readiness report fields; retain the existing frontend_apps meaning for apps selected for managed checks so consumers do not mistake discovery for executable configuration. Preserve the current strict managed check contract; do not fabricate coverage, equate build with build:bundle, equate test with coverage, or modify package.json scripts automatically.

Selected policy for this fix: report incomplete candidates with concrete remediation and do not generate their unavailable managed web checks by default. Existing complete apps continue to generate all supported checks. Explicit --frontend-app still validates required script/coverage contracts and errors clearly on unsupported input. Existing authored commands/components remain authoritative, so custom frontend actions are not rejected or rewritten by discovery. Keep package-manager evidence distinct from enabling installers or workflow jobs for an unconfigured candidate.

No prerequisites; unblocks jig-sh-so4.5. Validate focused frontend preview/validation regressions and final freshly built JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test.

title: Bound PR worker review-thread intents at parse time
description:
## Current state

Audited against master `4ef2e902` on 2026-09-07. parse_pr_worker_output iterates an unbounded reply array. Provider-facing schema maxItems and later actionable-ID limits do not bound unknown/duplicate intent evidence.

## Implementation

Pass the observed allowable reply count into the trusted parser and reject oversized arrays before per-entry projection or receipt construction. Retain total worker-output byte bounds, type validation and existing later mutation guards.

## Entry points

- `crates/jig/src/runtime/loops/pr_manager/worker_output.rs`
- `crates/jig/src/runtime/loops/pr_manager.rs`
- `crates/jig/src/runtime/loops/pr_manager/review_thread_budget_tests.rs`

## Validation

Run focused tests for the changed behavior, then build `cargo build -p jig-sh --bin jig` and use `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig work check --plan-id <implementation-plan>` for applicable repository gates. Finish backend changes with `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test`. Use generic isolated fixtures; no live services or credentials are required unless explicitly identified as an external prerequisite.

## Steps to Reproduce

Call parse_pr_worker_output with more reply intents than the observed allowed thread count, using valid nonempty unknown thread IDs and reply bodies; repeat with duplicate IDs. The parser currently accepts every entry despite schema maxItems.

## Acceptance Criteria

Reject oversized known, unknown and duplicate reply arrays before mutation and large evidence expansion. Zero-thread snapshots accept an empty array only. Exact-bound valid replies still work; malformed entries fail without posting.
acceptance_criteria: Reject oversized known, unknown and duplicate reply arrays before mutation and large evidence expansion. Zero-thread snapshots accept an empty array only. Exact-bound valid replies still work; malformed entries fail without posting.

description: Out-of-scope finding from the feat/jig-loop-iteration comprehensive review. The target-base PR classifier treats only fail and pending buckets as unhealthy; cancelled and unknown check conclusions fall through to observed-healthy cleanup, which clears repair attempt state even though CI has not demonstrated a successful terminal result. GitHub documents cancelled as a distinct non-success conclusion, while skipped and neutral can satisfy required checks. title: Make JSONL appends recover from partial writes
description:
## Current state

Audited against master `4ef2e902` on 2026-09-07. append_jsonl_locked still serializes directly to the file, appends a separate newline, and syncs afterward; failure can leave a damaged tail.

## Implementation

Serialize a complete bounded record before append. Hold existing writer authority across append/recovery and distinguish no-write, recoverable partial-write and sync-may-have-landed failures. A rollback may remove only bytes from this failed append, never historical records or a concurrent writer. Define fail-closed recovery when truncation/sync itself fails.

## Entry points

- `crates/jig/src/state/jsonl.rs`

## Validation

Run focused tests for the changed behavior, then build `cargo build -p jig-sh --bin jig` and use `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig work check --plan-id <implementation-plan>` for applicable repository gates. Finish backend changes with `JIG_DEV_BIN=target/debug/jig scripts/jig check test`. Use generic isolated fixtures; no live services or credentials are required unless explicitly identified as an external prerequisite.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use an isolated journal with one valid record. Inject a serializer failure after initial bytes, or a short write after part of the next record. The current append path can leave a partial tail that strict readers reject. Inject sync/rollback failures separately to distinguish corruption from ambiguous durability.

## Acceptance Criteria

Fault injection at serialization, short write, newline, sync and rollback proves prior records stay byte-identical and readable where recovery succeeds. Ambiguous durability is reported truthfully; no duplicate success receipt is invented. Concurrent writers and offset accounting remain correct.
acceptance_criteria: Fault injection at serialization, short write, newline, sync and rollback proves prior records stay byte-identical and readable where recovery succeeds. Ambiguous durability is reported truthfully; no duplicate success receipt is invented. Concurrent writers and offset accounting remain correct.
notes: Round 7 reconfirmed that the newer receipt-journal wrapper still inherits the pre-branch partial-append hazard: write failures and sync failures share one may-have-landed classification. Keep the remediation scoped to the existing Bead rather than the loop branch.

title: Deliver Jig Vault v3 cryptographic item access scopes
description:
<!-- BEAD:EPIC:BEGIN -->

Deliver Jig Vault v3 cryptographic item access scopes.

The epic replaces v2's one-passphrase/one-DEK/full-state security boundary with a
single portable v3 vault artifact containing signed policy over opaque item IDs
plus separately encrypted private-name descriptors and item bodies.

Human and machine principals own encrypted local identities.

Owners administer exact reader/writer item grants.

Every effective reader-set change rotates the wrapped item root, derives fresh
descriptor/body keys, and reseals both ciphertexts; writer/reader role-only
changes use signed authorization without rekeying.

The release includes partial unlock, rollback checkpoints, named identities,
accessible-only inventory, atomic onboarding and batch grants, capability checks,
policy/transfer dry-runs, local export freshness and redistribution guidance,
guided initialization, ordinary CLI and child-process adaptation, migration,
vault-only transfer, two-key registration proof, atomic principal replacement,
versioned portable/hardened identity KDF profiles, independent backup
passphrases, protected memory/core-dump suppression, additive OS keychain/Secure
Enclave/TPM2/FIDO2 identity protection, authenticated body/backup size buckets,
optional cover reseals, owner recovery resealing/readiness/verification/drills,
signed history rollover, TUI support, adversarial coverage, and operator
documentation.

It explicitly does not claim immediate online revocation, use-without-view,
remote audit authority, recipient forward secrecy after later HPKE-key
compromise, or protection from a reader who retained earlier plaintext.

It protects canonical item names from principals without current item access but
explicitly still leaks opaque envelope count/sizes, principal descriptors,
grants, and revision activity through the one complete artifact.

## Success Criteria

Completion requires B01 through B20 and the final integration acceptance in this
plan.

<!-- BEAD:EPIC:END -->

title: Add the vetted v3 cryptographic provider
description:
<!-- BEAD:B01:BEGIN -->

#### Outcome

Add the production cryptographic provider used by all later v3 work and prove the
selected RFC suites at the repository's Rust 1.88 floor.

This is a code-and-test deliverable, not a research-only spike.

#### Context

Jig currently uses Argon2id, XChaCha20-Poly1305, HKDF-SHA256, HMAC-SHA256, and
SHA-256.

V3 needs recipient-specific public-key wrapping and signatures.

The project plan selects RFC 9180 HPKE Base mode with X25519/HKDF-SHA256/
ChaCha20-Poly1305 plus strict Ed25519.

The preferred crates are `hpke` 0.14 and `ed25519-dalek` 3, subject to the exact
feature and MSRV proof in this bead.

#### Scope

Edit:

- workspace `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`;
- `crates/jig-vault/Cargo.toml`;
- a focused `crates/jig-vault/src/crypto_v3.rs` or equivalent owned module;
- crate module wiring;
- checked-in generic known-answer fixtures if needed;
- crate-level dependency/security comments and invariants where warranted.

Provide typed wrappers for:

- HPKE encryption-key generation;
- HPKE item-root-key seal and open;
- HKDF-SHA256 item-root expansion into non-interchangeable descriptor and body
  key types using canonical contexts;
- Ed25519 signing-key generation;
- strict sign and verify;
- SHA-256 fingerprints and revision hashes;
- domain-separated, length-prefixed preimage construction;
- zeroizing private-key representations;
- a page-dedicated non-growing `ProtectedMemory` owner for compact credentials
  and keys, plus Linux/macOS dump-disable and page-protection adapters.

Do not expose raw hazmat signing or unauthenticated ad hoc key-wrap helpers.

Disable default HPKE features and enable only `alloc`, `x25519`, and `chacha`.
Do not enable HPKE's `getrandom` feature; Jig already owns the fallible
`getrandom::fill` boundary and the dependency's convenience surface can panic on
`SysRng` failure.

Explicitly enable `x25519-dalek/zeroize` despite disabled transitive defaults,
and keep Ed25519 zeroization enabled. Prove the concrete HPKE secret-key wrapper
zeroizes on drop.

After fallible entropy acquisition succeeds, seed a private non-exhausting
`CryptoRng` compatible with `hpke` 0.14 and call only its `*_with_rng` paths for
key generation and encapsulation. Do not use a finite byte-buffer adapter whose
exhaustion can panic. Preserve the current `getrandom::fill` error behavior,
zeroize RNG seed/state where supported, and map failures to a stable vault error
without key bytes or partial output. If no compatible RNG can meet the Rust 1.88,
feature, zeroization, and panic-free constraints, stop and record the provider
decision rather than enabling HPKE's `getrandom` feature.

Do not enable ML-KEM, NIST curves, SSH, PEM, PKCS#8, age plugins, legacy Ed25519
compatibility, or hazmat features.

If the preferred crate versions cannot meet Rust 1.88, zeroization, advisory, or
feature constraints, stop before introducing a different wire suite and record a
concrete dependency decision in the implementation change.

#### Required tests

- RFC 9180 known-answer vectors for the exact selected ciphersuite.
- RFC 8032 Ed25519 vectors or upstream-compatible fixed vectors.
- Cross-process deterministic fixtures for public-key and signature decoding.
- Wrong recipient, wrong `info`, wrong AAD, ciphertext tamper, and signature
  tamper failures.
- Exact HKDF-SHA256 vectors prove the same item root and context derive stable
  keys, descriptor and body domains derive unequal keys, and any vault ID, item
  ID, epoch, suite, or purpose change changes the derived key.
- Provider APIs do not accept an item root where an AEAD content key is required
  and do not interchange descriptor and body key types.
- Strict length rejection; strict Ed25519 encoding rejection; canonical Jig
  X25519 descriptor encoding; alternate RFC 7748 encodings and all-zero shared-
  secret inputs.
- Debug output contains no private-key, item-root, derived-key, or HKDF-
  intermediate bytes.
- Drop/zeroization behavior is exercised where observable without unsafe test
  hooks.
- Linux and macOS protected-memory tests cover page rounding, guard pages, lock
  success/failure, dump exclusion, fork exclusion where supported, zeroize-
  before-unmap, and explicit degraded-mode state without reading freed memory.
- Core-size/dumpability controls activate before injected passphrase/provider
  capture; setup failure prevents the callback unless the explicit override is
  present.
- The resolved HKDF implementation's PRK/HMAC-state drop behavior is inspected
  and documented; root/derived output types zeroize even if internal provider
  state cannot make the same guarantee.
- A type/feature assertion proves the X25519 secret representation has drop
  zeroization with the resolved feature graph.
- Injected entropy failure makes key generation and encapsulation return a
  classified error without panic or partial output.
- The resolved HPKE feature graph omits `hpke/getrandom`, and the selected seeded
  RNG has no input-exhaustion panic path.
- `cargo tree -e features` demonstrates the intended feature closure.
- RustSec/advisory check has no unacknowledged applicable advisory.
- Rust 1.88 check builds the affected workspace targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

The new provider can wrap and unwrap a 32-byte item root key for one X25519
recipient, derive distinct descriptor and body keys through the exact typed HKDF
contexts, sign and strictly verify a domain-separated digest, and reject every
negative fixture without exposing private material.

The exact algorithm IDs, crate versions, feature set, licenses, MSRV result, and
dependency duplication decision are documented beside the code or in a concise
repository decision record consumed by later format code.

The resolved feature proof explicitly shows `x25519-dalek/zeroize`, omits
`hpke/getrandom`, and demonstrates that no OS-random failure or RNG-adapter
exhaustion reachable through Jig's provider wrapper can panic.

Compact provider/key material can enter only the protected allocation or an
explicitly reported degraded override; ordinary bulk/KDF allocations retain the
documented narrower guarantee.

`cargo test -p jig-vault`, strict crate Clippy, and the Rust 1.88 affected-target
check pass.

#### Dependencies and unblocks

Depends on no child bead.

Unblocks B02 and B03.

<!-- BEAD:B01:END -->
acceptance_criteria: Satisfy the Acceptance section in this issue description and keep every required test and compatibility check green.
notes:

title: Add identity principal item and access CLI administration
description:
<!-- BEAD:B10:BEGIN -->

#### Outcome

Expose the v3 identity and access lifecycle through typed CLI commands, safe
structured output, help, preflight, and end-to-end administrative tests.

#### Context

Core identity, policy, item-slot, and partial-session behavior exists from
B02/B04/B05/B07.

This bead supplies the operator workflows needed before ordinary data commands
can be exercised as different principals.

#### Scope

Update:

- `crates/jig/src/cli/vault.rs`;
- CLI conversion modules;
- `crates/jig/src/command/vault.rs`;
- `crates/jig/src/runtime/vault.rs` and focused modules;
- tool-definition constants;
- CLI output formatter/tests;
- help snapshots and consumer workflow tests.

Implement section 12 and 16 commands:

- named identity init/list/status/public/prove/passphrase change;
- identity protection status/enroll/rebind/remove and exact
  `portable|keychain|secure-enclave|tpm2|fido2` selection with opaque protector
  identifiers only;
- identity `--kdf-profile portable|hardened`, explicit downgrade gating, and
  public-header status that reports exact parameters and upgrade availability
  without unlocking or rewriting;
- exact one-identity selection through `--identity` or
  `JIG_VAULT_IDENTITY`, plus unambiguous `--identity-file` or
  `JIG_VAULT_IDENTITY_FILE`;
- principal challenge/add/replace/label/remove/grant-owner/revoke-owner with
  common dry-run;
- atomic principal add plus repeated initial reader/writer grants;
- access list `--me`, owner matrix, explain, check, singular grant/change/revoke,
  and repeated batch grant with common dry-run;
- explicit item create and repeated initial `vault init --item` flow;
- selected vault/identity/fingerprint headers on protected human interactions;
- dump/protected-memory setup before credential or protector prompts, persistent
  degraded-mode reporting, and the explicit emergency override contract;
- `privacy cover --item` with history/capacity/redistribution warnings;
- uniform inaccessible/nonexistent item-name result;
- stable access-check exit behavior;
- common authenticated mutation preview and stale-preview conflict;
- deterministic committed results with opaque revisions, redistribution
  recommendation, and exact transfer next step;
- `JIG_VAULT_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE` migration plumbing where command conversion
  owns it;
- `JIG_VAULT_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE` capture/plumbing for B15 without fallback to an
  identity or legacy vault passphrase;
- credential-variable removal before child-capable flows;
- interactive confirmations for revoke-all and multi-item owner removal;
- capacity preflight errors with exact rollover next steps;
- JSON fields and human summaries.

Validate public descriptors, IDs, roles, identity names/files, caller-supplied
item references, paths, and overwrite preconditions before passphrase capture
wherever possible.

Resolve authorization and persisted policy subjects only by full IDs.

Labels and shortened fingerprints are display conveniences and never mutation
selectors.

Never accept passphrases or private keys on argv.

No administrative command may reveal field values.

#### Required tests

- Clap parsing and rejection for every command and invalid role/path/combination.
- Named identity list/selection and no automatic private-key probing.
- Protected human output identifies the exact vault and selected identity.
- Identity public export and no private byte inclusion.
- Identity init/passphrase-change profile parsing, hardened opt-in, rejected
  silent downgrade, and stable status fields for profile/parameters/upgrade.
- Protection-mode/provider parsing, assurance/availability status without device
  invocation, two-factor enrollment/rebind, explicit removal downgrade, provider
  cancellation, and no fallback or secret argv/environment fields.
- Cover command requires write authority, produces no field output or public
  cover discriminator, and reports proof/headroom/redistribution cost.
- Challenge/proof binds the vault, owner, descriptor, HPKE ciphertext, recovered
  response, and candidate signature; wrong/missing/replayed proof rejects.
- Add developer plus Development/Staging grants in one policy revision and verify
  the developer cannot discover Production's name or decrypt retained pre-grant
  Development/Staging ciphertext.
- Batch grant is all-or-nothing and uses one policy revision.
- `access list --me` shows only accessible items and exact role capabilities.
- Owner matrix shows all decrypted names; non-owner cannot request the matrix.
- Explain/check do not read fields and use stable access exit behavior.
- Inaccessible Production and a nonexistent name have identical error/JSON
  shapes.
- Grant/revoke both report descriptor/body reseal and key-epoch changes;
  reader/writer-only changes report no rekey.
- Policy dry-run writes no vault, audit, checkpoint, or receipt bytes.
- Stale preview conflicts before mutation.
- External-credential-rotation warning and JSON flag on read revoke.
- Principal replacement transfers the exact authority set, rotates all readable
  items, removes old slots, and requires a different owner for owner replacement.
- Last owner and machine owner failures.
- Principal removal with outstanding access fails; explicit revoke-all succeeds
  after confirmation.
- Reserved environment variables are captured/removed correctly.
- V1/v2 commands retain old passphrase behavior.
- V3 passphrase alias reports identity target.
- Human and JSON output contain only permitted metadata.
- Every shared-state mutation reports local redistribution guidance without a
  delivery claim.
- Repeated init items produce encrypted descriptors and no public plaintext
  names.
- End-to-end workflow uses only generic principal names and items.

## Acceptance Criteria

An operator can create/select named human or machine identities, exchange a
public descriptor plus proof of both private keys, atomically onboard or replace
principals with exact grants, inspect and check only authorized item names,
preview and batch policy changes, manage owners safely, initialize private-name
items, and receive exact redistribution guidance through stable CLI and JSON
contracts.

No value-bearing output path is introduced.

`cargo test -p jig-sh`, relevant `jig-vault` tests, and strict CLI Clippy pass.

#### Dependencies and unblocks

Depends on B02, B04, and B07.

Unblocks B11, B12, B13, B14, B15, and B17.

<!-- BEAD:B10:END -->

title: Adapt field listing controlled read and injection to scopes
description:
<!-- BEAD:B11:BEGIN -->

#### Outcome

Make the existing field management, listing, controlled reveal, export, and
template injection CLI paths enforce v3 item access without changing their raw
output safety contracts.

#### Context

B08 provides authorized v3 mutations.

B10 provides selected identity and access administration.

This bead owns ordinary non-child data workflows and their structured metadata.

#### Scope

Adapt CLI/runtime paths for:

- field list/set/remove;
- compatible secret list/set/remove with exact canonical-name routing and
  owner-only fallback for unrepresentable legacy names;
- raw `vault read` stdout/private-file delivery;
- raw `vault inject` parsing, multi-item resolution, stdout/private-file delivery;
- accessible-descriptor catalog routing and accessible-only list JSON role
  metadata;
- v3 credential capture and selected identity resolution;
- access-aware audit events and safe failure stages.
- shared-mutation revision/redistribution results for field and compatible secret
  writes.

For injection, collect every distinct item and preflight access before resolving
any field or writing any byte.

Decrypt each referenced item at most once per authenticated operation.

Preserve:

- canonical reference syntax;
- pre-passphrase path/input validation;
- exact byte output with no newline;
- terminal `--reveal` requirement;
- hardened private-file sink rules;
- no structured raw-value output;
- concealed/text encryption and redaction meaning;
- operation lifecycle audit ordering.

#### Required tests

- Owner/writer can mutate an accessible item; reader/denied cannot.
- Inaccessible item contributes no list row, item name, count, timestamp, or field
  metadata.
- Item-specific list returns uniform unavailable before guessed field lookup.
- Read succeeds for reader/writer/owner and denies inaccessible/unknown/removed.
- Read error messages never confirm inaccessible item or field existence.
- Multi-item inject succeeds when all items are accessible.
- One denied item makes inject produce no stdout/file and no partial field
  resolution result.
- No list/read/inject JSON, audit, debug, or error contains the inaccessible
  Production fixture name.
- Repeated references decrypt one item once through an observable test seam that
  does not expose keys.
- Existing raw-output, symlink, hard-link, overwrite, terminal, size, and audit
  tests pass for v1/v2/v3.
- Secret commands enforce canonical item roles for representable names and owner
  access for unrepresentable legacy names.
- JSON/debug/error fixture scans contain no values or private material.

title: Adapt transparent exec and brokered run to scoped identities
description:
<!-- BEAD:B12:BEGIN -->

#### Outcome

Make child-process secret delivery enforce v3 access atomically before spawn and
strip all v3 credential variables without weakening existing process ownership,
redaction, or status behavior.

#### Context

`vault exec` is transparent streaming process plumbing.

`vault run` is a constrained broker for legacy names.

Their contracts are intentionally different and must remain separate.

#### Scope

Adapt:

- restricted dotenv reference resolution for `vault exec`;
- multi-item access preflight and one-revision field resolution;
- concealed-value redaction needle construction;
- v3 operation audit start/finish/failure metadata;
- child environment stripping for `JIG_VAULT_PASSPHRASE`,
  `JIG_VAULT_NEW_PASSPHRASE`, `JIG_VAULT_IDENTITY_PASSPHRASE`,
  `JIG_VAULT_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE`,
  `JIG_VAULT_ALLOW_UNPROTECTED_MEMORY`,
  `JIG_VAULT_IDENTITY`, `JIG_VAULT_IDENTITY_FILE`, and the non-secret but
  authority-shaping `JIG_VAULT_IDENTITY_HOME`;
- core-dump disable before secret resolution, protected parent credential/key
  pages excluded from fork, and inherited zero core-size limit for a child that
  receives plaintext;
- `vault run` exact canonical-name routing plus owner-only unrepresentable legacy
  access on v3;
- generic end-to-end v3 child fixtures.

Do not move child-process implementation into the policy layer.

Do not change transparent exec into the broker or give broker constraints to
exec.

Every referenced item and field must resolve before spawn.

Any denial, missing accessible field, signature failure, checkpoint rollback, or
redaction setup failure means no child starts.

#### Required tests

- Exec with accessible Development and inaccessible Production starts no child,
  leaves an explicit marker absent, and does not confirm Production's existence.
- Exec with several accessible items injects exact values from one authenticated
  vault revision.
- Reader can exec; writer and owner can exec; denied cannot.
- Concealed accessible values redact; text accessible values do not become
  redaction needles.
- Every reserved credential environment variable is absent in child probes.
- Injected dump/lock setup failure starts no child without explicit degraded
  override. Linux protected parent pages are absent after fork; macOS executes
  no user-controlled code before exec and has no protected mapping after exec.
  A secret-delivery child cannot produce an ordinary core image on either
  supported platform.
- Raw stdout/stderr streaming, inherited stdin/environment, nonzero/signal status,
  and no timeout/cap remain for exec.
- V3 run permits canonical names according to the addressed item role and permits
  unrepresentable legacy names only for owners.
- Existing broker timeout, cap, process-tree cleanup, temp-file wiping, and
  cleaned-environment tests stay green.
- Denied and nonexistent item names have identical pre-spawn behavior.
- Denied and failure audit events contain no guessed inaccessible item/field
  name or value.

## Acceptance Criteria

No v3 child starts until every secret input is authorized and resolved, and every
credential-control environment variable is stripped.

Existing transparent and brokered process contracts remain byte/status compatible
apart from intentional v3 authorization failures.

`cargo test -p jig-sh` with vault exec/run integrations, `cargo test -p
jig-vault`, and strict affected-crate Clippy pass.

#### Dependencies and unblocks

Depends on B08 and B10.

Unblocks B17 and B18.

title: Adapt 1Password import preview and commit to scoped items
description:
<!-- BEAD:B13:BEGIN -->

#### Outcome

Make the one-time 1Password dotenv import operate against one authorized v3 item
with metadata-safe preview and one atomic signed item revision.

#### Context

The current importer parses and validates before passphrase capture, previews
authenticated field collisions, resolves every external value, commits one field
batch, and installs a private destination file.

V3 must preserve that lifecycle without revealing an inaccessible destination's
item name or collision metadata.

#### Scope

Adapt CLI/runtime/core integration for:

- selected v3 identity;
- destination item existence and effective write role;
- owner-only item creation in the same transaction when explicitly requested;
- accessible-only previous-kind preview;
- revision-bound commit token/precondition;
- one item-body decrypt, batch mutation, reseal, signed revision, audit, and
  checkpoint update;
- safe committed-vault/destination-installation recovery reporting;
- committed vault-import result with previous/current revision and redistribution
  guidance;
- TUI backend-compatible preview types used later by B16.

Keep external `op` execution, bounds, raw diagnostic suppression, source parsing,
destination preflight, exact confirmations, and private file installation rules.

Dry-run invokes no `op` and makes no mutation.

An inaccessible or nonexistent destination returns the uniform unavailable
result before revealing any field collision or kind.

#### Required tests

- Writer and owner import into existing accessible item.
- Reader and denied principal fail before `op` execution and collision metadata.
- Owner explicit create-and-import path.
- Writer cannot create missing item.
- Dry-run invokes no resolver and reports only authorized metadata.
- Preview becomes stale after policy, role, key epoch, or destination item
  revision change.
- All external values resolve before one atomic item update.
- One failed resolver leaves vault and destination unchanged.
- Destination install race after commit reports committed action and exact safe
  rerun without values.
- Concealed-to-text confirmation remains `IMPORT TEXT`.
- Existing v1/v2 importer behavior and path/output hardening remain.
- Successful v3 commit recommends redistribution; dry-run and failed resolver do
  not.

## Acceptance Criteria

OnePassword import is fully usable by authorized v3 writers, reveals no
inaccessible item name or metadata, and retains its all-or-nothing vault update
and explicit post-commit destination recovery semantics.

`cargo test -p jig-sh`, `cargo test -p jig-vault`, import integrations, and
strict affected-crate Clippy pass.

title: Implement authenticated vault-only transfer and ancestry merge
description:
<!-- BEAD:B14:BEGIN -->

#### Outcome

Provide the supported developer/machine distribution path: signed vault-only
export, authenticated inspect/dry-run/status UX, trust-on-first-use absent
install, and safe same-vault ancestry merge with typed fork rejection.

#### Context

Transfer is not backup.

It contains the complete shared v3 ciphertext artifact, encrypted name
descriptors, and public opaque policy but no private identity, audit, or
checkpoint.

Independent item histories allow non-conflicting item progress to merge.

Policy forks and same-item forks do not auto-resolve.

#### Scope

Add a versioned bounded transfer codec in `jig-vault` plus CLI commands/runtime in
`jig-sh`.

Implement:

- transfer envelope magic/version, ID, timestamp, exporter, inner vault digest,
  public revision, and exporter signature;
- hardened output/input paths and total size cap;
- export from fully validated public v3 state without descriptor/body decryption;
- authenticated local export receipt after output commit;
- `transfer inspect` public delta/conflict output plus selected-identity
  accessible-name projection;
- `transfer import --dry-run` through the exact merge preflight with no writes;
- `transfer status` comparison of current versus last locally exported revision
  without delivery claims;
- absent-home import with selected identity membership check;
- default at-least-one-access requirement and explicit `--allow-no-access`;
- selected-identity accessible descriptor decrypt before first-use presentation;
- interactive genesis fingerprint confirmation;
- automation `--trust-genesis-fingerprint`;
- private absent-home staging/publication using existing supported guarantees;
- local audit/checkpoint initialization;
- existing-home same-vault import;
- policy equal/prefix/descendant checks;
- per-item equal/ancestor/descendant checks using complete proof chains;
- independent-item merge;
- tombstone handling under selected policy;
- selected-policy descriptor metadata/ciphertext validation and no independent
  descriptor merge outside its policy branch;
- one candidate validation and atomic write;
- redistribution recommendation when an existing-home merge produces a new local
  candidate not identical to the imported package;
- same-item/policy fork classified errors and recovery guidance;
- explicit rejection of a rollover lineage as a merge candidate for its source;
- transfer activity events.

Do not add `--force` or raw overwrite bypasses.

Do not trust package paths.

Do not include any `local/` file or selected identity bytes.

#### Required tests

- Exporter signature and vault digest verification.
- Package byte scan proves no identity private fixture, audit event, checkpoint,
  local receipt, plaintext item name, or plaintext value.
- Inspect without identity shows only opaque item deltas.
- Inspect with selected identity labels only descriptors it can decrypt.
- Dry-run predicts the same accepted merge/conflict as real import and writes no
  shared/local state.
- Export status covers never-exported, matching, and changed-since-local-export;
  no output claims distribution.
- Absent install with correct and incorrect genesis fingerprints.
- Selected registered/access/no-access/unknown principal cases.
- Identical existing import no-op.
- Incoming/local policy descendant cases.
- Independent Development and Staging updates merge.
- Unrelated policy advance plus still-authorized stale item writer merges.
- Concurrent advance by a writer removed in the selected policy rejects.
- Concurrent item advance from an older key epoch rejects after selected-policy
  rekey.
- Two Production children of one parent reject as same-item fork.
- Divergent policy journals reject.
- Local checkpoint prevents rollback.
- Different vault ID/genesis rejects.
- A valid signed rollover bridge does not make its new lineage mergeable with the
  source lineage.
- Malformed/oversized/aliased/symlinked input/output rejects before credential
  capture where applicable.
- Injected staging/publication failures preserve documented absent/retry states.
- A novel merged state recommends re-export; no-op and dry-run do not claim a
  mutation.
- Human/JSON output contains only public metadata plus names decrypted for the
  selected identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Two generic developers can inspect and dry-run exchange of one v3 artifact,
merge independent item changes, track only local export freshness, and
cryptographically reject unauthorized, stale, or forked state when prior
checkpoints provide the evidence without disclosing inaccessible item names.

The transfer is demonstrably incapable of restoring a private identity by itself.

`cargo test -p jig-vault`, `cargo test -p jig-sh`, transfer integration tests,
and strict affected-crate Clippy pass.

#### Dependencies and unblocks

Depends on B04, B05, B06, B07, and B10.

Unblocks B16, B17, B18, and B20.

<!-- BEAD:B14:END -->
